narrative.markdown:
Consist in a tag associated to another component (buttons, tabs in the nav, avatar or icons) to visually indicate information associated to the paired element.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Used to inform,

•	the number of associated items to the paired element (e.g. number of applied filters, number of unread notifications, …)

•	a characteristic of the paired element (e.g. new associated with a tab, channel icon associated with an avatar, …)

![Badge container example — Overview](/assets/badge-container/overview.png)

### Anatomy

![Badge container example — Anatomy](/assets/badge-container/anatomy.png)

1. **Paired element** - The component that the BadgeContainer is connected to
2. **Tag**

### Variants

The BadgeContainer component doesn’t have different sizes, colors, and modifiers, however, the associated [Tag](/components/core/tag/) can assume all tag component sizes, colors, and modifiers.

![Badge container example — Variants](/assets/badge-container/variants.png)

#### States

Despite the BadgeContainer using the component Tag, which is interactive, the Tag component should always remain in the default state because the BadgeContainer paired element could be interactive (e.g. button).

#### Position

The BadgeContainer can assume different positions always on top of the paired element. Usually, it is used on the right of the paired element.

![Badge container example — Variants Position](/assets/badge-container/variants-position.png)

### Guidelines

#### Use cases

The BadgeContainer component can be used in multiple use cases, such as used to inform,

##### the number of associated items to the paired element

![Badge container example — Use cases the number of associated items to the paired element: number of applied filters](/assets/badge-container/element-number-of-applied-filters.png)
*number of applied filters*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*number of associated items*

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/86f1ac-badgecontainer) — Design tab, image 6.*

![Badge container example — Use cases the number of associated items to the paired element: number of unread notifications](/assets/badge-container/element-number-of-unread-notifications.png)
*number of unread notifications*

##### a characteristic of the paired element

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*channel icon associated with an avatar*

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/86f1ac-badgecontainer) — Design tab, image 8.*

![Badge container example — Use cases a characteristic of the paired element: new associated with a tab](/assets/badge-container/element-new-associated-with-a-tab.png)
*new associated with a tab*

### Resources

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > BadgeContainer`

* [BadgeContainer component](https://www.figma.com/file/OAai6yfKydI1p4afnUUI6V/2B---%F0%9F%93%96-Core-documentation-A-%3E-L?type=design\&node-id=1421%3A381588\&mode=design\&t=Vktyc5rRlh55wYJf-1) — Core component library
* [BadgeContainer handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?type=design\&node-id=279%3A175865\&mode=design\&t=OYdQrmIqXnoHEMYC-1) — Handoff guidelines

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Introduction

The BadgeContainer component is used to visually represent and group related badges or labels within a user interface. It provides a concise and organized way to convey additional information or highlight specific attributes associated with an element or content.

### Tone and voice

Maintain a consistent tone and voice when writing for the Badge Container component. Consider the context and purpose of the badges, and ensure the language aligns with the overall tone and voice of the rest of your product. The tone can be informative, friendly, or directive, depending on the specific use case.

### Word choice

Use language that is concise, easily understandable, and aligned with the user's expectations. Avoid jargon or technical terms unless your target audience is familiar with them.

Choose clear and descriptive words like "New" and "Favorite".

### Numbers and maximum numbers

##### Informative tags

The number of items (issues, emails, conversations) assign to you, the limit of characters on a text area, the number of items you're creating, etc.

* Show all characters
* Limit of 7 characters
  * 1
  * 12
  * 123
  * 1,234
  * 12,345
  * 99,999+
* For unlimited characters, no label is needed.

##### Counter tags

The number of filters applied, the number of items in tables, etc.

* Show up to 3 characters
  * 1
  * 12
  * 99+

### Concise and clear writing

Keep the content within badge labels brief and to the point. Users should be able to grasp the information quickly without excessive reading or interpretation.

### Variants

Consider different variations of the Badge Container component, such as different badge styles, sizes, or positioning. Coordinate with the visual design to ensure the badges align with the overall user interface.

### Best practices

![Do example](/assets/badge-container/dos-and-don-ts-do.png)
*Do*
Number of filters applied

![Do example](/assets/badge-container/dos-and-don-ts-do-2.png)
*Do*
Number of emails unread

**Do:** Country code
![Do example](/assets/badge-container/dos-and-don-ts-do-3.png)

**Don't:** The + is placed on the left side of the number
![Don't example](/assets/badge-container/dos-and-don-ts-dont.png)

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

* Announce the badge content (e.g. an `aria-label` like "3 unread").
* Don't rely on color or position alone to convey meaning.

For accessibility guidance that applies to every component, see
[Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
DatePicker is the Cobalt Marketplace date picker, built on the Cobalt core Calendar. Cobalt core has its own [DatePicker](/components/core/date-picker/): a separate package with a different API.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The design guidance for date pickers is on the Cobalt core [DatePicker](/components/core/date-picker/) page. Its own props and examples are in the Code tab. For a date range, see [DateRangePicker](/components/marketplace/daterangepicker/).

#### Against the guidance

Checked against the package source (DateRangePicker shares the same code):

* **An inline calendar only.** There is no input and no popup, so opening below the input (or above
  it when there is no room) is up to the page, for example with an InputGroup and a StatefulPopup.
* **Navigation is off by default.** The previous and next month buttons, the month selector and the
  year dropdown appear only with `withNavigation` and a list of `availableYears`.
* **The current date is not marked by default.** Set `highlightToday`.
* **Ranges with invalid dates** work as the guidance says: a range can span disabled days, which stay
  disabled. Telling the user those days are excluded is up to the page.
* **The 30-day range limit** is not built in; the page has to enforce it and show the message.
* **Width** follows the container, as the guidance says.

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Writing guidelines

This component follows the core page's content guidelines. For copy rules that apply everywhere, see
[Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

The accessibility guidance is on the core [DatePicker](/components/core/date-picker/) page. Checked against
this package's source (both known gaps are in the Code tab):

* The previous and next month buttons are icon-only and have no accessible name.
* The year dropdown has no label: the component does not pass one, and offers no prop to set it.
* The month buttons show the selected month visually only.
* The day grid comes from the Cobalt core Calendar; it was not checked here.

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
DragAndDrop enables the user to upload a file by dragging it to an area of the screen.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Anatomy

![Drag and drop example — Anatomy](/assets/drag-and-drop/anatomy.png)

1. **Illustration**. The illustration should be used but is optional when at least one file was already dragged or in small viewports. Should not be used different illustrations.
2. **Title**. The title is mandatory and should be consistent for all use cases.
3. **Button**. The button is mandatory and enables the user to upload the file without dragging it.
4. **Description**. The description is mandatory and should show the file's max size.

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are three sizes available (Large, Medium, and Small), each to be applied to the respective viewport.

![Drag and drop example — Variants Sizes: Large](/assets/drag-and-drop/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Sizes: Medium](/assets/drag-and-drop/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Sizes: Small](/assets/drag-and-drop/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

#### States

![Drag and drop example — Variants States: Default](/assets/drag-and-drop/states-default.png)
*Default*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants States: Focused](/assets/drag-and-drop/states-focused.png)
*Focused*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants States: Error](/assets/drag-and-drop/states-error.png)
*Error*

![Drag and drop example — Variants States: Hover-drag](/assets/drag-and-drop/states-hover-drag.png)
*Hover-drag*

#### Modifiers

The illustration should be used but is optional when at least one file was already dragged or in small viewports.

It is highly recommended to have an associated label. When necessary, the label should have the button and/or link to download the template and see guidelines aligned on the right.

![Drag and drop example — Variants Modifiers: With illustration](/assets/drag-and-drop/modifiers-with-illustration.png)
*With illustration*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Modifiers: Without illustration](/assets/drag-and-drop/modifiers-without-illustration.png)
*Without illustration*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Modifiers: With label](/assets/drag-and-drop/modifiers-with-label.png)
*With label*

#### Alignment

The DragAndDrop is always placed vertically and horizontally in the center of the container.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/94ce34-draganddrop) — Design tab, image 15.*

### Guidelines

#### Group

When combined with other components it follows the same rules applied to forms, distanced by 16px of each input with label.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/94ce34-draganddrop) — Design tab, image 16.*

#### Placement

The DragAndDrop is usually used inside a Modal but can be placed inside different components or on a page.

![Drag and drop example — Guidelines Placement: Inside a modal](/assets/drag-and-drop/placement-inside-a-modal.png)
*Inside a modal*

  ![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Inside a form*

  ![Drag and drop example — Guidelines Placement: Inside a panel](/assets/drag-and-drop/placement-inside-a-panel.png)
*Inside a panel*

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/94ce34-draganddrop) — Design tab, image 18.*

#### Use cases

The amount of supported file types influence the button and the description copy.

Visit the [Content tab](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/94ce34-draganddrop/b/8277c8) to learn more.

### Behavior

#### Interaction

##### General experience

In this section we will show the general DragAndDrop flow, however, it can be different depending on the use case.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience](/assets/drag-and-drop/interaction-general-experience.png)

* Start

The Drag\&Drop component has;

**Label**. The label indicates that this is a mandatory field. It also enables the user to Download the template (button) to promote the success of the file upload and also to see the guidelines (link) aligned on the right.

**Illustration**.

**Title**.

**Button**. The button shows all valid file types and enables the user to upload the file without dragging.

**Description**. The description shows the file max size.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Start](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-start.png)
*Start*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Start - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-start-small-viewport.png)
*Start - small viewport*

* Error

If the user interacts with the primary actions without a valid file dragged the DragAndDrop component state changes for Error with an error hint visible.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Error: Required](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-error-required.png)
*Error: Required*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Error: Required - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-error-required-small-viewport.png)
*Error: Required - small viewport*

* Focused

Using the keyboard the user can change the DragAndDrop component state for Focused, focusing the button to select a file to upload.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Focused](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-focused.png)
*Focused*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Focused - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-focused-small-viewport.png)
*Focused - small viewport*

* Dragging file(s)

When the user drags the file to the droppable area, this area changes to give feedback to the user.

If it is a valid file type the DragAndDrop component state changes for Hover-drag.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Dragging file](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-dragging-file.png)
*Dragging file*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Dragging file - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-dragging-file-small-viewport.png)
*Dragging file - small viewport*

* Loading

When the user drops a valid file the file uploading starts. The file upload can happen immediately after the file is selected/dropped or only after a few seconds. During this period a spinner, with the message “Uploading your file”, provides the feedback that the file is uploading.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Loading file](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-loading-file.png)
*Loading file*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Loading file - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-loading-file-small-viewport.png)
*Loading file - small viewport*

* Invalid file(s) dragged

After the loading, if the file is invalid an error message appears between the Label and the DragAndDrop explaining the error and requesting to upload a new file. Different errors can be shown, such as:

When a file larger than the max size is dragged, the error message shows “Your file can't exceed 5 MB. Please upload a new one.”. The max size should be adapted to the use case.

When an unaccepted file type is dragged, the error message shows “Your file type must be CSV or JSON. Please upload a new one.”. The file type(s) should be adapted to the use case.

When an empty file is dragged, the error message shows “Your file must have valid data. Please upload a new one.”.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Invalid file(s) dragged](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-invalid-file-s-dragged.png)
*Invalid file(s) dragged*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Invalid file(s) dragged: Large file - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-invalid-file-s-dragged-large.png)
*Invalid file(s) dragged: Large file - small viewport*

* File dragged

After the loading, if the file is valid, a card that represents the dragged file is created. The card can have up to two actions. The delete action is mandatory. The other action is dependent on the use case and can change the file, preview the file or other.

When multiple files uploading is available, the DragAndDrop component is also available to upload more files.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: File dragged](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-file-dragged.png)
*File dragged*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: File dragged - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-file-dragged-small-viewport.png)
*File dragged - small viewport*

* Importing the file

After all fields are filled the user can import the file by interacting with the primary action. During the importing the primary action state change for feedback and the card's actions are disabled.

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Importing the file](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-importing-the-file.png)
*Importing the file*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Importing the file - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-importing-the-file-small-viewport.png)
*Importing the file - small viewport*

* Importing error

If the importing was not succeeded an error message appears bellow the correspondent Card explaining the error and requesting to upload a new file. The error message can vary depending on the use case but as a general message, it can show “We couldn’t upload your file. Please try again or upload a new one.”

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Importing error](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-importing-error.png)
*Importing error*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: Importing error - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-importing-error-small-viewport.png)
*Importing error - small viewport*

* File imported

If the importing was succeeded a toast appears. The toast message can vary depending on the use case but as a general message it can show “xxxxxxxxxx”

![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: File imported](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-file-imported.png)
*File imported*

  ![Drag and drop example — Interaction General experience: File imported - small viewport](/assets/drag-and-drop/experience-file-imported-small-viewport.png)
*File imported - small viewport*

#### Spacing

The spacing between,

* the illustration and the title depends on the viewport, L:16px / M:12px / S:8px.
* the title and the button is always 16px.
* the button and the description is always 8px.

![Drag and drop example — Variants Spacings: Spacing - Large](/assets/drag-and-drop/spacings-spacing-large.png)
*Spacing - Large*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Spacings: Spacing - Medium](/assets/drag-and-drop/spacings-spacing-medium.png)
*Spacing - Medium*

  ![Drag and drop example — Variants Spacings: Spacing - Small](/assets/drag-and-drop/spacings-spacing-small.png)
*Spacing - Small*

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Introduction

The DragAndDrop component allows users to click and drag items within a designated area and drop them in another area. This component is commonly used for tasks like moving or uploading files.

### Tone and voice

Be concise, clear, and instructional. The language should be straightforward and easy to understand.

### Word choice

Use words that describe the action of dragging and dropping, such as **"drag"** and **"drop".** Avoid using synonyms for the same action, as it can be unclear to the user.

### Concise and clear writing

Provide clear instructions on how to use the DragandDrop component - where to click and how to drag and drop the item.

Be clear about what type of file is accepted. Inform the user about the maximum upload size, using the appropriate [unit of measurement](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/23fa55-grammar-and-mechanics/t/5282bf).

### Variants

The amount of supported file types influence the button and the description copy.

##### Up to two supported files,

* the supported file types should be described in the button
* the max file size should be described in the description

##### For more than two supported files,

* the supported file types typology (e.g. audio) should be described in the button
* the max file size and the supported file types should be described in the description

### Examples

narrative.markdown:
Headers are applied on the top of a page, card, modal or panel and are used to identity them.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Only use headers for the **top heading** of the page. If you need to use headers to create sections within a page, use a [**Section Header**](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header/t/650c9d) instead.

### Anatomy

1. **PreTitle**

3. **Heading Title**
4. **Description**
5. **Divider**

![Header example — Variants Modifiers: With Description Action](/assets/header/modifiers-with-description-action.png)
*With Description Action*

### Guidelines

#### Group

The header should be combined with different components, as the following examples show.

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Simple Header - Medium](/assets/header/group-simple-header-medium.png)
*Simple Header - Medium*

  ![Header example — Guidelines Group: Simple Header - Small](/assets/header/group-simple-header-small.png)
*Simple Header - Small*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Simple Header - Large](/assets/header/group-simple-header-large.png)
*Simple Header - Large*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Actions - Medium](/assets/header/group-header-with-actions-medium.png)
*Header with Actions - Medium*

  ![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Actions- Small](/assets/header/group-header-with-actions-small.png)
*Header with Actions- Small*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Actions - Large](/assets/header/group-header-with-actions-large.png)
*Header with Actions - Large*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav - Medium](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-medium.png)
*Header with Nav - Medium*

  ![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav- Small](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-small.png)
*Header with Nav- Small*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav - Large](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-large.png)
*Header with Nav - Large*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and Toolbar - Medium](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-toolbar.png)
*Header with Nav and Toolbar - Medium*

  ![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and Toolbar- Small](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-toolbar-2.png)
*Header with Nav and Toolbar- Small*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and Toolbar - Large](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-toolbar-3.png)
*Header with Nav and Toolbar - Large*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar - Medium](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-multiple.png)
*Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar - Medium*

  ![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar- Small](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-multiple-2.png)
*Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar- Small*

![Header example — Guidelines Group: Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar - Large](/assets/header/group-header-with-nav-and-multiple-3.png)
*Header with Nav and multiple Toolbar - Large*

##### Headers with and without borders

By default, headers come with a visible bottom border. In this case, they follow the general spacing rules.

However, if you use borderless headers, the spacing below should be reset to **0px**.

![Header example — Group Headers with and without borders](/assets/header/group-headers-with-and-without-borders.png)

##### Used with a nav, toolbar or section headers

When used with any of these components, they should be snapped together (**no spacing**). Make sure also to remove the header’s bottom border when using with the Nav component.

![Header example — Group Used with a Nav, Toolbar or Section Headers](/assets/header/group-used-with-a-nav-toolbar.png)

#### Placement

The main page header should always be placed at the top of the page and have full width.

![Header example — Guidelines Placement](/assets/header/guidelines-placement.png)

#### Use cases

##### Multiple actions

Multiple actions can be combined in the header. These actions have different hierarchies and the following guidelines should be applied,

* Before a destructive action or a Toggle, a Divider should always be used.
* Between secondary/primary actions and tertiary actions, a Divider should always be used.
* When there is more than one secondary action, a primary outlined style should be used.
* The max. amount of visible actions is 5 (excluding the more option action), and 50% of the header width is the max. width for actions.
* When an action is hidden, all actions from the same hierarchy and below should also be hidden.

*See some examples below.*

| **Hierarchy**       | **Style**                                                                                                       | **Quantity**     | **Divider**                                                                       | **Visibility**            |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| More options action | Always secondary transparent.                                                                                   | Is unique.       | *N/A*                                                                             | Is always visible.        |
| Primary action      | Always primary filled.                                                                                          | Is unique.       | Always use a divider after the primary action if there are any secondary actions. | Is always visible.        |
| Secondary actions   | Secondary filled when there is only one secondary action.Primary outlined there are multiple secondary actions. | Can be multiple. | Always use a divider after the secondary actions group.                           | Can be visible or hidden. |
| Tertiary actions    | Always transparent.                                                                                             | Can be multiple. | Always use a divider before the tertiary actions group.                           | Can be visible or hidden. |
| Toggle              | *N/A*                                                                                                           | Can be multiple. | Always use a divider before the group of toggles.                                 | Can be visible or hidden. |
| Destructive action  | Always error transparent.                                                                                       | Is unique.       | Always use a divider before.                                                      | Can be visible or hidden. |

##### Divider

Before a destructive action or a Toggle, a Divider should always be used.

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Destructive action](/assets/header/divider-destructive-action.png)
*Destructive action*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Destructive action - open](/assets/header/divider-destructive-action-open.png)
*Destructive action - open*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Toggle](/assets/header/divider-toggle.png)
*Toggle*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Toggle - open](/assets/header/divider-toggle-open.png)
*Toggle - open*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Toggle and destructive action](/assets/header/divider-toggle-and-destructive-action.png)
*Toggle and destructive action*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Toggle and destructive action - open](/assets/header/divider-toggle-and-destructive-action-open.png)
*Toggle and destructive action - open*

Between a secondary/primary actions and tertiary actions, a Divider should always be used.

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Tertiary action](/assets/header/divider-tertiary-action.png)
*Tertiary action*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: Tertiary action - open](/assets/header/divider-tertiary-action-open.png)
*Tertiary action - open*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: 2 secondary and 1 tertiary actions](/assets/header/divider-2-secondary-and-1-tertiary.png)
*2 secondary and 1 tertiary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Divider: 2 secondary and 1 tertiary actions - open](/assets/header/divider-2-secondary-and-1-tertiary-2.png)
*2 secondary and 1 tertiary actions - open*

##### Style

When there is more than one secondary action should be used primary outlined style

![Header example — Use cases Style: multiple secondary actions](/assets/header/style-multiple-secondary-actions.png)
*multiple secondary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Style: multiple secondary actions - open](/assets/header/style-multiple-secondary-actions-open.png)
*multiple secondary actions - open*

##### Visibility

5 is the max amount of visible actions (excluding the more option action) and 50% of the header width is the max width for actions.

When an action is hidden all actions from the same hierarchy and below should be also hidden.

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 3 tertiary actions](/assets/header/visibility-3-tertiary-actions.png)
*3 tertiary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 3 tertiary actions - open](/assets/header/visibility-3-tertiary-actions-open.png)
*3 tertiary actions - open*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 5 tertiary actions](/assets/header/visibility-5-tertiary-actions.png)
*5 tertiary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 5 tertiary actions - open](/assets/header/visibility-5-tertiary-actions-open.png)
*5 tertiary actions - open*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 3 secondary and 2 tertiary actions](/assets/header/visibility-3-secondary-and-2-tertiary.png)
*3 secondary and 2 tertiary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 3 secondary and 2 tertiary actions - open](/assets/header/visibility-3-secondary-and-2-tertiary-2.png)
*3 secondary and 2 tertiary actions - open*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 5 secondary and 1 tertiary actions](/assets/header/visibility-5-secondary-and-1-tertiary.png)
*5 secondary and 1 tertiary actions*

![Header example — Use cases Visibility: 5 secondary and 1 tertiary actions - open](/assets/header/visibility-5-secondary-and-1-tertiary-2.png)
*5 secondary and 1 tertiary actions - open*

#### Headers vs section headers

Section headers are similar to headers, but they have slightly different inner padding. They should be used to separate sections inside the page.

##### On the page

Section headers should follow the same rules as normal headers. When placed on the page, the first header should be placed right after the main header (**0px**) even if the main header has a toolbar or a nav below.

Remember to use a logical tree of headings. Every main section should use an **H2** section header. Sub-sections inside them should use **H3**, **H4**, and so on.

Section headers should not have the bottom border unless you need it for a very specific reason. They should also always be full-width. The content within each section, however, should follow the global rules of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px** horizontal padding.

At the end of a section, we usually add a divider at **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px** below the last element of that section. If you don’t want dividers, just keep the same spacing of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px** from the next section.

![Header example — Headers vs Section headers On the page](/assets/header/headers-vs-section-headers-on-the.png)

##### On panels

On panels the guidelines are mostly the same, the only difference is to use H4 headers instead.

![Header example — Headers vs Section headers On panels](/assets/header/headers-vs-section-headers-on-panels.png)

##### Headers and dividers

Some forms have headers and dividers inside to create logic groups. Main sections should be displayed with an **H2 section header** (without a border) followed by its form fields (on panels use **H4 section header** instead). The spacing between the header and the first label is **0px**.

The header is full-width, but the contents of each section follow the general rules. So the lateral padding should be **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**.

By the end of each section, we’ll have a divider that is **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px** below the last element of the section. The next section’s header should be snapped to the previous divider (**0px**).

Here’s some examples on different viewports:

![Header example — Headers vs Section headers Headers and dividers: Section headers and dividers - Small viewport](/assets/header/dividers-section-headers-and-dividers-small.png)
*Section headers and dividers - Small viewport*

![Header example — Headers vs Section headers Headers and dividers: Section headers and dividers - Large viewport](/assets/header/headers-vs-section-headers-on-the.png)
*Section headers and dividers - Large viewport*

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

In large and medium viewports the header should always be fixed on top. For small viewports, the header could be fixed or not, depending on the use case.

The actions associated to the header could be fixed or not, placed on the top or in the bottom, depending on the interaction.

##### User needs to interact with elements before interacting with the actions:

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Medium. Fixed header.*

Viewport: Medium

Header: Fixed

Actions: Non-fixed. Placed on the bottom, below the content.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 69.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Large. Fixed header.*

Viewport: Large

Header: Fixed

Actions: Non-fixed. Placed on the bottom, below the content.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 68.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Small. Non-fixed header.*
Viewport: Small; Header: Non-fixed; Actions: Non-fixed. Placed on the bottom, below the content.

  ![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Small. Fixed header.*
Viewport: Small; Header: Fixed; Actions: Non-fixed. Placed on the bottom, below the content.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 70, image 71.*

##### User doesn't need to interact with any of the elements or needs to interact with one/limited elements before interacting with the action:

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Medium. Fixed header.*

Viewport: Medium

Header: Fixed

Actions: Fixed on top, attached to the header.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 73.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Large. Fixed header.*

Viewport: Large

Header: Fixed

Actions: Fixed on top, attached to the header.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 72.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Small. Non-fixed header.*
Viewport: Small; Header: Non-fixed; Actions: Fixed on the bottom, detached from the header.

  ![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Small. Fixed header.*
Viewport: Small; Header: Fixed; Actions: Fixed on top, attached to the header.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 74, image 75.*

#### Interaction

When a vertical scroll is applied and the header is fixed on top, a scroll shadow to the header must be applied.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/85a3f8-header) — Design tab, image 76.*

#### Text truncation

The header title and description should never be truncated. If the title and/or the description has a significant amount of text, it should be multi-lined, as the following examples show.

![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Title - Medium](/assets/header/truncation-long-title-medium.png)
*Long Title - Medium*

  ![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Title - Small](/assets/header/truncation-long-title-small.png)
*Long Title - Small*

![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Title - Large](/assets/header/truncation-long-title-large.png)
*Long Title - Large*

![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Description - Medium](/assets/header/truncation-long-description-medium.png)
*Long Description - Medium*

  ![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Description - Small](/assets/header/truncation-long-description-small.png)
*Long Description - Small*

![Header example — Behavior Text truncation: Long Description - Large](/assets/header/truncation-long-description-large.png)
*Long Description - Large*

#### Spacing

Headers follow the general rules of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px** for the space inside the header.

![Header example — Variants Spacing: Spacing - Small](/assets/header/spacing-spacing-small.png)
*Spacing - Small*

  ![Header example — Variants Spacing: Spacing - Medium](/assets/header/spacing-spacing-medium.png)
*Spacing - Medium*

  ![Header example — Variants Spacing: Spacing - Large](/assets/header/spacing-spacing-large.png)
*Spacing - Large*

narrative.markdown:
A LabeledIcon is a component that combines an icon with a label.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Anatomy

![Labeled icon example — Anatomy](/assets/labeled-icon/anatomy.png)

1. Icon
2. Label

### Variants

#### Sizes

![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: Micro](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-micro.png)
*Micro*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: XSmall](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-xsmall.png)
*XSmall*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: Small](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: Medium](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: Large](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Sizes: XLarge](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-xlarge.png)
*XLarge*

#### Colors

By default the label color is Secondary 800, however, as the icon, it can have different colors applied.

![Labeled icon example — Variants Colors: icon and label secondary800](/assets/labeled-icon/colors-icon-and-label-secondary800.png)
*icon and label secondary800*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Colors: icon info700 and label secondary800](/assets/labeled-icon/colors-icon-info700-and-label-secondary800.png)
*icon info700 and label secondary800*

  ![Labeled icon example — Variants Colors: icon and label info700](/assets/labeled-icon/colors-icon-and-label-info700.png)
*icon and label info700*

### Guidelines

#### Group

The distance between two LabeledIcons or a LabeldIcon and another component (e.g. divider) should be **8px**.

![Labeled icon example — Guidelines Group](/assets/labeled-icon/guidelines-group.png)

#### Use cases

A LabeledIcon should be used when an icon needs to be combined with a label and it could be used in and/or combined with several other components, such as:

![Labeled icon example — Guidelines Use cases: in the header to highlight the section](/assets/labeled-icon/cases-in-the-header-to-highlight.png)
*in the header to highlight the section*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*combined with inputs as a hint*

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/5465d3-labeledicon) — Design tab, image 13.*

![Labeled icon example — Guidelines Use cases: in table cells to show the status](/assets/labeled-icon/cases-in-table-cells-to-show.png)
*in table cells to show the status*

#### Dont’s

A LabeledIcon is not an interactive component and should never be used for that purpose.

Please also consider checking the [Color | Color usage](https://zeroheight.com/51aaf6147/p/49728f/b/94c676) page when applying different colors in LabeledIcons.

#### Link vs button vs LabeledIcon

A link should never be used with an icon.

To use an interactive component with an icon and a label, the button component should be applied.

To use a non-interactive component with an icon and a label, the labeledicon component should be applied.

![Labeled icon example — Link vs Button vs LabeledIcon: Link](/assets/labeled-icon/labeledicon-link.png)
*Link*

  ![Labeled icon example — Link vs Button vs LabeledIcon: Transparent button with icon](/assets/labeled-icon/labeledicon-transparent-button-with-icon.png)
*Transparent button with icon*

  ![Labeled icon example — Link vs Button vs LabeledIcon: Labeledicon](/assets/labeled-icon/sizes-micro.png)
*Labeledicon*

| **Component** | **Interactive** | **Icon**                 | **Size**                               | **Font size**                                                                         | **Label weight**             |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| LabeledIcon   | False           | True                     | Micro XSmall Small Medium Large XLarge | Micro: Small XSmall: Medium Small: Medium Medium: Medium Large: Medium XLarge: Medium | Optional (Regular or Medium) |
| Button        | True            | Optional (True or False) | Medium Small XSmall                    | Medium: Medium Small: Small XSmall: N/A                                               | Medium                       |
| Link          | True            | False                    | Medium Small                           | Medium: Medium Small: Small                                                           | Regular                      |

### Resources

Find this component under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > LabeledIcon`

* [LabeledIcon component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?node-id=1048%3A145579\&t=uKxaIEgOvsWKrXlT-1) — Core component library
* [LabeledIcon handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=3%3A15267\&t=sGMnhaBvne0ZUrQV-1) — Handoff guidelines

narrative.markdown:
Nav is a Cobalt Marketplace component built on the Cobalt core [Tab](/components/core/tab/) component: the row that holds a set of tabs.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The design guidance for Nav is on the Cobalt core [Tab](/components/core/tab/) page: Nav is built on it and follows the same guidelines. Its own props and examples are in the Code tab.

Nav adds three things to a row of core `Tab`s:

* **Overflow.** When the tabs are wider than their container, the row scrolls horizontally and shows navigation buttons on the right (`scrollSnap` sets the scroll step).
* **Divider.** An optional divider under the row (`divided`).
* **One size for every tab.** `size` is set once on `Nav` and applied to each `NavTab`.

### Code

### Content

### Writing guidelines

Tab labels follow the [Tab](/components/core/tab/) content guidelines. For copy rules that apply
everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

Each `NavTab` is a core `Tab`, so the [Tab](/components/core/tab/) accessibility guidance applies: wrap
the `Nav` in a `<nav>` landmark and mark the selected tab with `aria-current="page"`. `Nav` does not do
either for you.

The navigation buttons shown on overflow are icon-only and have no accessible name, so a screen reader
announces them only as "button". There is no prop to label them yet; see the known gap in the Code tab.

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
Pagination is the Cobalt Marketplace pagination. Cobalt core has its own [Pagination](/components/core/pagination/): a separate package with a different API.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The design guidance for pagination is on the Cobalt core [Pagination](/components/core/pagination/) page. Its own props and examples are in the Code tab.

#### Against the guidance

Checked against the package source:

* **Matches:** previous and next buttons, page buttons, a non-interactive "…" for truncated pages, labels
  only on medium and large viewports (`variation="labels"`), 4px between actions, and "Previous" / "Next"
  labels you can override.
* **Not available:** the "Jump to" action in the anatomy, and the three sizes: buttons are always small,
  and the viewport only decides whether labels show.
* **Not enforced:** the fixed 48px height (the component is as tall as its 32px buttons) and the 2, 4 or
  6 page buttons (`maxPagesCount` takes any number).

The core Pagination has the "Jump to" action ("Go to") and a page-size selector.

### Writing guidelines

This component follows the core page's content guidelines. For copy rules that apply everywhere, see
[Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

The accessibility guidance is on the core [Pagination](/components/core/pagination/) page. Checked against
this package's source:

* It renders a `<nav>`; give it an `aria-label` when a page has more than one.
* The current page is marked `aria-current="true"` rather than `"page"` (a known gap, in the Code tab).
* Page buttons are named by their number only, and nothing announces the new position when the page
  changes. The core Pagination does both.

narrative.markdown:
SearchInput is the Cobalt Marketplace search field, built on the Cobalt core [Input](/components/core/input/) component. Cobalt core has its own [SearchInput](/components/core/search-input/): a separate package with a different API.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The design guidance for search fields is on the Cobalt core [SearchInput](/components/core/search-input/) page, and this package follows it. Its own props and examples are in the Code tab.

What this package adds to a core `Input`:

* A search icon at the start and, with `dismissable`, a clear icon at the end once there is text.
* `onSearch`, called with the current value after the user stops typing for `triggerDelay` milliseconds (300 by default), and with an empty string when the field is cleared.
* `UnstyledSearch`, the same field without the input frame, for placing inside another component.

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Writing guidelines

Placeholder and label copy follow the [Input](/components/core/input/) content guidelines (Search fields). For copy rules
that apply everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

The core [SearchInput](/components/core/search-input/) accessibility guidance applies. Two things in this
package need care until they are fixed (both listed as known gaps in the Code tab); the core SearchInput
has neither problem:

* **The field's accessible name.** SearchInput sets `aria-label` to the text typed so far, after your
  own props, so an `aria-label` you pass is replaced and an empty field has no name. Name it with a
  visible `<label>` linked by `id`, or with `aria-labelledby`.
* **The clear icon is not a button.** It responds to a mouse click only: keyboard users cannot reach
  it, and it has no accessible name. Keyboard users can still clear the field by deleting the text.

The field already uses `type="search"`.

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).
narrative.title: SearchInput

narrative.markdown:
Tooltip is the Cobalt Marketplace tooltip, built on the Cobalt core [Popup](/components/core/popup/) component. Cobalt core has its own [Tooltip](/components/core/tooltip/): a separate package with a different API.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The design guidance for tooltips is on the Cobalt core [Tooltip](/components/core/tooltip/) page, and this package follows it. Its own props and examples are in the Code tab.

What this package adds to a core `Popup`:

* Showing and hiding on hover of a trigger: wrap the trigger as `children`, or pass `triggerRef`.
* Text from `label` (one line, truncated with an ellipsis) or custom `content`.
* Placement with the `Position*` exports (centred above the trigger by default), kept inside the viewport by capping the tooltip's width.
* The `variation` colors: `theme` (default), `light`, `dark` and `error`.

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Writing guidelines

Tooltip copy follows the core [Tooltip](/components/core/tooltip/) content guidelines. For copy
rules that apply everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

The accessibility requirements are on the core [Tooltip](/components/core/tooltip/) page; the core Tooltip
meets them. This package does not yet (all three are listed as known gaps in the Code tab), so until it does:

* **Keyboard.** It opens on mouse hover only, not on focus, so keyboard users never see it. Do not put
  information only in a tooltip.
* **Esc.** There is no Esc handling to close it.
* **ARIA.** It sets no `role="tooltip"` and cannot be linked to its trigger with `aria-describedby`:
  its props type accepts no `role` or `id`. Make sure the trigger's own accessible name, or text on the
  screen, carries the same information.

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
Composed of related items, vertically organized, that can be collapsed or expanded. When collapsed only the item title is shown. When expanded also the item content is visible.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Accordions are used when the user needs to deal with a large amount of content that can be grouped into related items. The accordion interaction enables the user to see all component content progressively by groups which help the user to process the information.

### Anatomy

![Accordion anatomy: collapsed item, item title, item arrow, expanded item, item content](/assets/accordion/anatomy.png)

1. **Collapsed item**
2. **Item title**
3. **Item arrow**
4. **Expanded item**
5. **Item content**

### Variants

#### Styles

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### States

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Modifiers

Each accordion item has an arrow that, when visible, can have different positions.

![Arrow: default position](/assets/accordion/arrow-default.png)
*Arrow: default*

  ![Arrow: inline position](/assets/accordion/arrow-inline.png)
*Arrow: inline*

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Quantity

Accordions can have as many items as needed.

![Accordion with many items](/assets/accordion/quantity.png)

### Guidelines

#### Group

The spacing between accordions on the page should follow the global rules of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**.

![Grouped accordions spaced apart following the global spacing rules](/assets/accordion/usage-group.png)

### Behavior

#### Interaction

Accordions can have two main interactions distinguished by the number of items that can be opened simultaneously. In both cases, the item arrow changes when the item is open.

##### Single item open

In this interaction when one item is expanded and upon expanding a different one, the first will automatically collapse. There’s only one item expanded at a time. Expanding the following item should close the previous one automatically.

This is the ideal accordion interaction that should be used whenever possible.

![Single item open interaction, where expanding an item collapses the previously open one](/assets/accordion/interaction-single-item-open.png)

##### Multiple items open

In some use cases, we can have multiple accordion items opened. This interaction should be carefully used because the users may deal with a massive amount of content, which could decrease their experience.

![Multiple items open interaction, where more than one item can be expanded at the same time](/assets/accordion/interaction-multiple-items-open.png)

#### Text truncation

The accordion item title is single-lined because it is inside a rectangular shape with a fixed height. For that reason must be truncated when needed.

The accordion item content should never be truncated because its container height grows to accommodate all content.

![Accordion item with a truncated title](/assets/accordion/text-truncation.png)

#### Spacing

Accordion content has a consistent inner padding of 12px.

![Accordion content with a 12px inner padding](/assets/accordion/spacing.png)

#### Dimensions

Accordions have `width=100%`. Additionally, an optional maximum width of **620px** can be set.

![Accordion set to an optional maximum width](/assets/accordion/dimensions-maxwidth.png)

### Resources

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Accordion`

* [Accordion component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?type=design\&node-id=192%3A16157\&t=LFDEEZ7VR7CSc7m6-1) — Core component library
* [Accordion handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?type=design\&node-id=378%3A204079\&t=R0lvmGNtaRi2cFSA-1) — Handoff guidelines

### Code

### Installation

> **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Examples

### Content

### Writing guidelines

This component has no component-specific copy rules yet. For copy rules that apply
everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

#### Development

* Make each header a focusable control that toggles `aria-expanded`.
* Link each header to its content region via `aria-controls` so it expands/collapses by keyboard.

For accessibility guidance that applies to every component, see
[Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
A circular shape that should represent a user, an object, or an entity, among others.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The Avatar is a pretty straightforward component to use when you want to represent people and things in a visual way. It can have multiple sizes and colors for the background and the content inside, and it can contain letters (up to two), icons, or images as its content.

### Anatomy

![Avatar anatomy: icon, text, image, status, border](/assets/avatar/anatomy.png)

1. **Icon** - Consider using by following our [Assets library](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/32d352-icons/b/346276)
2. **Text** - Indicates the initials of a user's name
3. **Image** - Any specific picture
4. **Status** - Indicates if a user is available, away, focused, or busy
5. **Border** - Always present to support the layout

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are five size variations. The default is the medium size but you may choose to use any other size to fit your layouts.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Types

![Primary avatar type](/assets/avatar/type-primary.png)
*Primary*

  ![Light-Primary avatar type](/assets/avatar/type-light-primary.png)
*Light-Primary*

  ![Basic avatar type](/assets/avatar/type-basic.png)
*Basic*

  ![Picture modifier avatar](/assets/avatar/modifier-picture.png)
*Picture*

#### Colors

You can find more guidelines about color usage [here](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/49728f-color/b/94c676).

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### States

![Default state avatar](/assets/avatar/state-default.png)
*Default*

  ![Hover state avatar](/assets/avatar/state-hover.png)
*Hover*

  ![Active state avatar](/assets/avatar/state-active.png)
*Active*

  ![Focused state avatar](/assets/avatar/state-focused.png)
*Focused*

#### Modifiers

The content can be composed of text (max 2 characters), an icon (any icon from our [Asset library](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/32d352-icons/b/346276)), an image, or any combination with a status associated.

![Text modifier avatar](/assets/avatar/modifier-text.png)
*Text*

  ![Icon modifier avatar](/assets/avatar/modifier-icon.png)
*Icon*

  ![Picture modifier avatar](/assets/avatar/modifier-picture.png)
*Picture*

  ![Avatar modifier combined with a status indicator](/assets/avatar/modifier-with-status.png)
*With Status*

#### Status

Avatars can display the status by applying a status icon to the bottom right corner of the element. For the specific Talkdesk use case, we have statuses with different correspondent colors:

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

Also note that due to accessibility concerns (color blindness), we can add a shape to identify the different statuses.

![Available status with an accessible shape](/assets/avatar/status-shape-available.png)
*Available*

  ![Away status with an accessible shape](/assets/avatar/status-shape-away.png)
*Away*

![Busy status with an accessible shape](/assets/avatar/status-shape-busy.png)
*Busy*

  ![Offline status with an accessible shape](/assets/avatar/status-shape-offline.png)
*Offline*

### Guidelines

#### Group

You can combine multiple Avatars together using the AvatarGroup pattern. Stacks can be used to group a list of users, objects, or entities in one element.

We can set a maximum number of 3 avatars to stack. When the maximum value is reached, it displays a counter next to the stack with the remaining number of items.

![A single standalone avatar](/assets/avatar/group-standalone.png)
*Standalone*

  ![Three stacked avatars with a +4 overflow counter](/assets/avatar/group-avatargroup.png)
*AvatarGroup*

#### Placement

Elements that officially use the Avatar component:

![Avatar next to a ChatBubble message](/assets/avatar/placement-chatbubble.png)
*ChatBubble message*

  ![Avatars used as a List item](/assets/avatar/placement-list.png)
*List item*

  ![Do example](/assets/avatar/placement-table.png)
*Table item*

#### Use cases

Whenever possible, an image should be used to represent a user, but if an image is unavailable, one or two letters can be used instead.

If the record name contains **two (or more) words**, like first and last name, the first capitalized letter of the first and the last names should be used. For records that only have a **single word** name, only the first capitalized letter should be used.

If either an image or initials are unavailable (e.g. a phone number), the user icon should be used as a fallback. There are other situations where we might think of adding fallbacks, for example on a call from an "Unknown Number". This should generate an icon instead of the "UN" initials.

Different icons can be set as a fallback for each object. For example, users can have the "user" icon as a fallback and for companies, we could use the "building" icon.

**Do:** Use the initials (one or two), an icon, or an image to represent an entity. If the entity doesn't have a name (e.g. a phone number), use an icon representative of that entity (e.g. "user")
![Do example](/assets/avatar/usecases-do.png)

**Don't:** Don't use more than two characters and avoid empty avatars. Also, try not to use circular icons and don't change the default color.
![Don't example](/assets/avatar/usecases-dont.png)

##### Product references

![Avatar used inside a Table, in an admin seat-management list](/assets/avatar/productref-inside-table.png)
*Inside a Table*

![Avatar used inside a List of actions](/assets/avatar/productref-inside-list.png)
*Inside a List*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*Inside a ChatBubble*

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/44fb82-avatar) — Design tab, image 43.*

##### Using a BadgeContainer

An Avatar in a table can also have both a Status element and an Icon, when applying the BadgeContainer, that represents the Channel.

![Avatars combined with a status and a channel icon via BadgeContainer](/assets/avatar/badgecontainer.png)

##### Using an interactive avatar

PhoneApp has a specific use case that involves an interaction in the Avatar to represent that a customer is calling.

![An interactive avatar used in a message example](/assets/avatar/interactive-avatar.png)

#### Best practices

##### Colors

![Do example](/assets/avatar/placement-table.png)
*Do*
We should use the light primary avatar color to display users in a list. This way we will have a consistent look and feel whenever we are displaying user avatars.

![Do example](/assets/avatar/do-s-don-ts-colors-do.png)
*Do*
For other objects, we can use any other color by picking one from the quick list or use a custom one as long as it follows the accessibility guidelines regarding the use of color.

Please consider checking the [Color | Color usage](https://zeroheight.com/51aaf6147/p/49728f/b/94c676) page when applying different colors.

##### Status

Avatars can also display the user's status by applying a status icon to the right bottom corner of the element.

**Do:** When displaying the user’s status, use an alternative textual or visual representation.
![Do example](/assets/avatar/do-s-don-ts-status-do.png)

**Don't:** Do not trust color alone for status because that will not be accessible by color-blind users.
![Don't example](/assets/avatar/do-s-don-ts-status-dont.png)

##### Badges

Avatars can be used in combination with tags (using the BadgeContainer pattern) to display a badge. Badges can be placed on the top right corner of the element.

**Do:** The tag size is adjusted based on the avatar size, but the positioning remains always the same.
![Do example](/assets/avatar/do-s-don-ts-badges-do.png)

**Don't:** Don't apply different sizes and/or positions.
![Don't example](/assets/avatar/do-s-don-ts-badges-dont.png)

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

This component has defined variation sizes that shouldn't change based on the viewport size.

#### Interaction

Besides our Avatar [states](/components/core/avatar/), you can find specific assets in the [Phone Library](https://www.figma.com/file/IZCC3x71w1meRON8FcKgjb/Phone-Desktop-Library?type=design\&node-id=0%3A1\&mode=design\&t=g7APqeQOlFQQmJvw-1) that are related to reference when a customer is calling.

#### Overflow

Regarding the text variation, you shouldn't exceed the limit of two characters. Consider always the first and last name initials.

#### Loading

The [Skeleton](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/avatar--basic#skeleton) is intended to give visual feedback on the component while data is in a loading state.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

You can apply the skeleton behavior when loading an Avatar.

#### Internationalization

Depending on the language, the generation of initials may be tricky. For Latin, Greek, or Cyrillic alphabets it's easy to extract the first letter of the names to generate the initials, however, not all languages are this linear.

For example, in Chinese, the name “Mao Zedong” is written as “毛泽东” (no spaces). So the initials could be “毛泽” or just “毛“. The problem of using initials is that in Chinese this can generate a different word with a meaning that is totally different than the intended. So, in this case, the two initials “毛泽” would mean "Mao Ze"; but using only one “毛“ would mean "hair".

Other languages may have similar problems, so, for now, we should limit the generation of initials to Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic.
