narrative.markdown:
Buttons are used primarily for actions. Examples include Add, Save, Delete, and Sign up. Each page should have one primary button, and a Return or Enter keyboard event should trigger it. Any remaining calls-to-action should be represented as secondary buttons.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Anatomy

![Icon before label](/assets/button/icon-label.png)
*icon+label*

A button has a container, a label, and an optional icon placed before or after the label as a
child element rather than through a dedicated prop.

### Variants

The most common are rectangular buttons with rounded corners, that are easily identifiable and look
good next to the input field. Choosing the right style for the button will depend on the purpose,
platform, and guidelines. Each variant below is rendered live from the published package.

#### Sizes

* Three sizes available: Tiny, Small and Medium.
* Pressing a button should be a simple task and if a user is unable to successfully tap on a button
  or in the process tap on a neighbouring element by mistake, it will lead to a negative experience
  and loss of time.
* For most platforms, consider making touch targets at least 98px x 42px. A touch target of this
  size results in physical size of about 11mm, regardless of screen size. The recommended target
  size for touchscreen elements is at least 7–10mm.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Types

Button ships 9 types: Primary, Secondary, Info, Danger, Warning, Success, Feature, MonoDark, and
MonoLight. Independently of type, each can also be shown outlined or transparent (see Styles
below).

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

MonoDark is for light surfaces and MonoLight for dark ones, in each style:

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Styles

Styles are primarily used to differentiate more important actions from less important ones. Create a
hierarchy of actions that will guide the user where there are multitudes of choices. Usually, you can
have a single prominent button (that style is often called "primary"), and several medium
"secondary" and low emphasis "tertiary" actions.

Filled is the default style, shown under Types above. Outlined and transparent:

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### States

Creating correct interactions and styles for your buttons is one of the most important parts of the
process. Each state must have clear affordances that distinguish it from other states and the
surrounding layout but should not drastically alter a component or create a lot of visual noise.

* **Default:** communicates that the component is interactive and enabled.
* **Hover:** the user has placed a cursor above it.
* **Focused:** it's ready to be interacted with, for example after tabbing to it.
* **Active:** the user is pressing it.
* **Feedback (pending):** the action isn't immediate, and the button shows that it's in progress.
* **Disabled:** it's currently non-interactive but can be enabled later.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Guidelines

#### When to use

* For the main action on a view, such as Save, Send, or Submit: one primary button per view, and
  secondary buttons for the supporting actions.
* For multiple related actions, group them together. See Button group below.

#### When not to use

Do not use buttons as navigational elements. Instead, use links when the desired action is to take
the user to a new page.

#### Buttons vs links

Buttons communicate actions that users can take. They are typically placed throughout your UI, in
places like Dialogs, Forms, Toolbars, etc. The distinction between buttons and links matters:

* Links are used when you're navigating to another place, such as: "view all" page, "Roger Wright" profile, etc.
* Buttons are used when you are performing an action, such as: "send," "merge," "create," "upload," etc.

![A link next to buttons](/assets/button/buttons-vs-links.png)

#### Icon-only buttons

Contained buttons can place icons next to text labels to both clarify action and call attention to a
button.

![Icon-only button](/assets/button/icon-only.png)
*icon*

![Icon after label](/assets/button/label-icon.png)
*label+icon*

Check icons documentation.

### Behavior

#### Max width and truncation

Buttons have a max width of 300px, independent of the button size.

We don't recommend using a truncated label using ellipsis (...) inside buttons because it's
important to have a clear and visible message for the action. If you have large content and/or can't
control the character limitation, you need to limit the width of the button and orient the user to
keep the copy simple.

#### Button group

When using groups of buttons together, they need to have a distance between them. This distance
depends on the type and size of the buttons. There are also some components that require you to use a
predefined button size (e.g. Page Headers use regular buttons; Toolbars and Section Headers use
small-sized buttons).

**Regular size buttons.** For regular buttons, the distance between them should be 12px. This should
be applied in headers, footers, or any other place where two or more buttons are placed side by side.
It should also include any dividers in between.

![Regular buttons spaced 12px apart](/assets/button/group-regular-12px.png)

**Small buttons.** For small buttons, the spacing is usually 4px between them. Small buttons are
normally used in toolbars or table cells as icons.

![Small buttons spaced 4px apart in a toolbar](/assets/button/group-small-4px.png)

There is however one exception. In the event that you would need to add more than one button (not
transparent) to a Section Header or a Card Header, the spacing should be the same as for regular size
buttons (12px). Transparent buttons should keep the same 4px spacing.

![Section header with 12px and 4px button spacing](/assets/button/group-header-exception.png)

### Split button

Split buttons are used to pair one primary action with one or more closely related secondary actions. They look like two buttons merged together, separated by a divider in the middle: the first segment triggers the main action, and the second segment opens a dropdown with the related actions. In code it is the `SplitButton` export of the Button package.

Use a split button when you have two or more related actions but one of them is clearly more relevant and used more often than the others. The most common action lives on the first segment so it can be triggered in a single tap, while the less frequent variations are tucked into the dropdown. Do not use a split button when the actions are unrelated, or when they are equally important — in those cases use separate buttons or a regular dropdown instead.

#### Variants

A split button is always made of two parts: a first action and a last action that opens a dropdown arrow. Both segments are visually joined with a divider in the middle and read as a single, related unit. The first and last action always share the same button type, so the two segments never mix types or styles within the same split button.

##### Sizes

Split buttons support the same sizes as buttons: Tiny, Small and Medium.

Because a split button is made of two tappable segments, both segments must remain comfortable to press. As with regular buttons, consider making touch targets at least 98px x 42px for most platforms. A touch target of this size results in a physical size of about 11mm, regardless of screen size. The recommended target size for touchscreen elements is at least 7–10mm. The dropdown segment should never become so narrow that it is hard to tap accurately.

##### Types

Split buttons reuse the same button types available in the system. Because the first and last action always share the same type, selecting a type applies it to the whole split button rather than to a single segment. Each type is available in the same outlined and text-only versions, including the MonoDark and MonoLight variants.

##### Styles

This button is only available in the filled style.

##### Icons

Just like contained buttons, the first action of a split button can place an icon next to its text label to clarify the action and call attention to it.

* icon
* icon+label

The last segment always shows the dropdown arrow, which signals that additional related actions are available.

**Icons** Check icons documentation.

#### Guidelines

##### Group

When placing split buttons alongside other buttons or split buttons, treat the whole split button as a single unit and keep the same spacing rules used for buttons. The distance depends on the type and size of the buttons, and some components require a predefined size (e.g. Page Headers use regular buttons; Toolbars and Section Headers use small-sized buttons).

**Regular size buttons** For regular sizes, the distance between a split button and the next button should be 12px. This applies in headers, footers, or any other place where two or more buttons are placed side by side, including any dividers in between. The divider inside the split button is not affected by this spacing — it belongs to the component.

**Small buttons** For small sizes, the spacing is usually 4px between elements. Small split buttons are normally used in toolbars or table cells.

As with buttons, there is one exception: if you need to add more than one non-transparent button or split button to a Section Header or a Card Header, the spacing should match the regular size (12px). Transparent variants keep the 4px spacing.

##### Placement

Choosing a split button over a related component depends on how the actions relate to one another:

* **Split button** — Use when there is one clearly dominant action plus a small set of closely related variations of it (e.g. Save vs Save and publish). The dominant action is one tap away; the variations are in the dropdown.
* **Button** — Use when there is a single action and no closely related variations. If you would only ever have one item in the dropdown, use a plain button.
* **Dropdown / Menu button** — Use when all the actions are roughly equal in importance and there is no obvious primary action to surface on its own. A split button is the wrong choice when no single action stands out.

##### Use cases

This component should be used when the actions that the user will have are related. The most used and relevant action should be visible in the first part of the split button and might or might not be on the more options menu of the second part. Depending on the context.

##### Best practices

Don't use this button for additional non related features. For that porpouse use a button group with more options icon.

Don't use this button in outline or transparent styles.

#### Behavior

##### Responsiveness

The split button always remains the same, respecting the responsiveness needed by the page. It might hide the label and be just an icon and a dropdown depending on the needs.

The responsiveness for the split button generally follows the responsiveness of normal buttons.

##### Interaction

###### Focus

The two segments of a split button can be focused independently. The first action and the dropdown segment each receive focus on their own, so users navigating by keyboard can reach the main action and the dropdown separately, with clear focus affordances on whichever segment is active.

##### States

Each segment of a split button must have clear affordances that distinguish its state from the surrounding layout, without creating visual noise. States apply per segment, so the first action and the dropdown segment can be in different states at the same time (for example, one focused while the other is at rest).

* **Default** — Communicates that the segment is interactive and enabled.
* **Hover** — When a user has placed a cursor above the segment.
* **Focused** — Communicates that the segment is currently on and ready to be interacted with. Each segment can be focused independently.
* **Active** — Communicates that the user has tapped on the segment.
* **Feedback** — Used when an action is not performed immediately, communicating that the segment is in the progress of completing the action.
* **Disabled** — Communicates that the segment is currently noninteractive but can be enabled in the future.

##### Text truncated

As with buttons, we don't recommend truncating the first action's label with an ellipsis (...), because the action needs to stay clear and visible. If you have large content and/or can't control the character limitation, limit the width of the split button and keep the copy simple instead of relying on truncation.

##### Theming

Follow the same approach as Button.

##### Dark mode

Follow the same approach as Button.

##### Internationalization

Follow the same approach as Button.

##### Dimensions

Split buttons follow the same max width of 300px as buttons, independent of size. This width covers the whole component, including the first action, the divider, and the dropdown segment.

### Related components

* **Link:** use Link instead of Button when the action navigates to another page or view.
* **[Split button](#split-button):** for a primary action paired with a small set of related, lower-frequency
  alternatives shown in a dropdown.

### Writing guidelines

* Button labels should be concise and clear enough to indicate the next action to the user. Avoid unnecessary words and articles such as *the*, *an*, or *a*.
* Use active verbs or phrases that clearly indicate an action (e.g., *Save*, *Send*, *Cancel*). Avoid *No*/*Yes* or *OK*.
* The primary button is on the right side and the secondary button is on the left.
* Use sentence case.
* Don't use punctuation, special characters or symbols.
* Make interactive elements consistent in identification and functionality. Don't label a search button *Send* on one page and *Enter* on another.
* Buttons with icons should be used to add clarity and to stand out in the UI. When adding icons to a button, make sure they are relevant and match the intended action.
* Make sure that buttons that are icon-only have appropriate labels on hover or tooltips.

**Prefer single verb+noun over verb+adjective or adjective+noun**

**Do:** Use “Create flow”.
![Do example](/assets/button/do.png)

**Don't:** Avoid “Create new flow” or “New flow”.
![Don't example](/assets/button/dont.png)

**Do:** Use action verbs.
![Do example](/assets/button/content-do-action-verbs.png)

**Don't:** Avoid "Yes" and "No".
![Don't example](/assets/button/content-dont-yes-no.png)

### When to use

* **Accept:** when the user needs to confirm they've read critical or legally binding information, or when it's legally required to have the user's consent.
* **Add:** when the user is adding something new to a list or group (e.g., contact, team, set, disposition, integration, agent).
* **Apply:** when the user applies a filter or a date for a call.
* **Call:** when the user needs to make a call.
* **Change:** when the user needs to change the password.
* **Clear:** when the user needs to clear filters from a list or search.
* **Create:** when the user wants to create something from scratch (e.g., dashboard, flow, function, role).
* **Delete:** when the user wants to delete something and that action is irreversible.
* **Dismiss:** when the user wants to dismiss non-critical messages that might appear in the UI.
* **Download:** when the user needs to download files, images, reports, etc. from the app/product.
* **Edit:** when the user needs to change or correct information that they've added before.
* **Explore:** when the user wants to explore or know more about something (e.g., AppConnect, pricing).
* **Filter:** when the user wants to add specific criteria to filter information or a search.
* **Got it:** when the user needs to confirm they've read the information that isn't critical or legally binding.
* **Hide:** when the user needs to hide something (e.g., the keypad, rows, or columns in a table).
* **Log in:** please use Sign in instead.
* **Next:** when the user wants to move forward to the next page or item.
* **Previous:** when the user wants to go back to the previous page or item.
* **Remove:** when the user wants to remove something from a list, when the action is easily reversible or not critical.
* **Request:** when the user needs to request something (e.g., a demo, support, training).
* **Resolve:** when the user needs to resolve something (e.g., voicemails).
* **Save:** when the user is saving something they've created or edited, and changes will be effective immediately.
* **Search:** when the user wants to search for something (e.g., phone numbers, contacts, ring groups).
* **Send:** when the user needs to send/submit something.
* **Sign in:** when the user needs to sign in to Talkdesk or to one of our products.
* **Submit:** Please use Send instead.
* **Skip:** when the user wants to skip an optional step or task (e.g., walkthrough).
* **Upload:** when the user needs to upload files, images, reports, etc., to the app/product.
* **Confirm:** when the user wants to confirm information like an address or a phone number.
* **View:** when the user needs to view full documents, articles, or news.

### Links

* Links should be as descriptive and specific as possible and make sense in isolation.
* Links should be sincere and predictable, they should always tell the user what will happen or what they’ll find when they click on it.
* Start with the most important terms.
* Avoid one-word links. Users with poor motor skills might have trouble selecting them.
* Don't write *Click here*, *Read this* or *Learn more*, as they're not clear, specific, or accessible. Ask about what the link does, where it takes the user or what it shows to them: answer these questions before, then start writing.
* For links that lead to information, the link should be the text about that information (e.g., *Visit our* *support page* *for more information*).
* For links that lead to a page where the user can perform a task, always start with a verb (e.g., *Create article*).
* Use sentence case.
* Don't include ending punctuation. **Exception:** when the link is a question, it should include the question mark.
* Don't include articles in the link (e.g., *Read our* *Terms of Service*\*,\* not *Read* *our Terms of Service*).
* If you have to refer to a link, say *click the link* and not *follow the link*.
* For links with icons, place the icon to the left side of the link. **Exception:** for RTL (Right-to-Left) languages, such as Arabic and Hebrew, icons should appear to the right of links.

### Accessibility

### Interactions

#### Mouse

Activating a button with a mouse click triggers its action the same way as pressing Enter or Space.
No additional guidance beyond a native `<button>` element's default behavior applies here.

#### Keyboard

* Users should be able to navigate to any action button by using normal keyboard navigation (tab key).
* Buttons should display a visible focus state when users tab to them.

If using the keyboard, the expected behavior:

| Key   | Action                    |
| ----- | ------------------------- |
| Tab   | Moves focus to the button |
| Enter | Activates the button      |
| Space | Activates the button      |

### Considerations

#### Design

* 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)
* 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)

See the Design tab's States section for the button's visible focus-ring treatment.

#### Development

Depending on the button type we can have two ARIA roles that should be used. These should be applied
to the title of the button.

For regular, secondary, success and danger buttons, which usually have advisory information for the
user that is not important enough to justify an alert, we should use the `status` role
(documentation).

However, for danger messages which are often used to communicate an important and usually
time-sensitive message to the user, we should use the `alert` role (documentation).

* **Use standard markup.** Avoid using `<div>` or `<img>` tags to create buttons. Screen readers don’t automatically know either is a usable button.
* The `button` has an accessible label. By default, the accessible name is computed from any text content inside the button element. However, it can also be provided with [aria-labelledby](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#aria-labelledby) or [aria-label](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#aria-label).
* If a description of the button's function is present, the button element has [aria-describedby](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#aria-describedby) set to the ID of the element containing the description.
* **Screen readers handle buttons and links differently.** When styling links to look like buttons, remember that screen readers handle links slightly differently than they do buttons. Pressing the Space key triggers a button, but pressing the Enter key triggers a link.

Icons may be used as visual labels (without visual text) if the meaning of the icon is visually
self-evident and if there is a programmatically associated semantic label available to assistive
technologies, normally this can be accomplished by using an `aria-label`.

![Code sample: a button labelled only by a filter icon, with aria-label Filters](/assets/button/code-icons-as-labels.png)

```html
<button aria-label="Filters">
  <span class="fa fa-filter"></span>
</button>
```

### How to test the component

* Tab to the button using only the keyboard and confirm it receives a visible focus ring.
* Activate it with both Enter and Space and confirm the same action fires either way.
* With a screen reader running, confirm the button announces a clear, accurate accessible name.

Calendar is a Cobalt core component.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Calendar is the date grid that date pickers are built on. Date-picking guidance is on the [DatePicker](/components/core/date-picker/) page. Calendar's own props and examples are in the Code tab.

narrative.markdown:
Cards can be used to contextualize and group sets of information. Each card can have its own title and actions that are only applied to the card's contents.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

This can help create individual sets of information that can be manipulated independently from the rest of the page content.

### Anatomy

![Card anatomy: header, content, footer](/assets/card/anatomy.png)

1. **Header**. The Card header is usually an H3 Header.
2. **Content**
3. **Footer**

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are three sizes available (Large, Medium, and Small), each to be applied to the respective viewport.

![Large card size](/assets/card/size-large.png)
*Large*

  ![Medium card size](/assets/card/size-medium.png)
*Medium*

  ![Small card size](/assets/card/size-small.png)
*Small*

#### Styles

Cards are simple containers for content and interactions. The **Card** can have a different type (outlined) due to style distinctions and divergent interaction patterns.

Therefore they will have similar behaviors, properties, and usage.

By default, cards are elevated through a shadow with no outline.

![Default card, elevated with a shadow and no outline](/assets/card/style-default-card.png)
*Default card*

  ![Outlined card](/assets/card/style-outlined-card.png)
*Outlined card*

##### Cards inside another card

Cards inside another card should always (for all viewports),

* be used in the outlined card variant
* be spaced by 8px
* have 12px padding

![Outlined cards nested inside another card, spaced 8px apart with 12px padding](/assets/card/cards-inside-card.png)

#### States

![Default state](/assets/card/state-default.png)
*Default*

  ![Active state](/assets/card/state-active.png)
*Active*

  ![Focused state](/assets/card/state-focused.png)
*Focused*

![Hover state](/assets/card/state-hover.png)
*Hover*

  ![Selected state](/assets/card/state-selected.png)
*Selected*

  ![Pressed state](/assets/card/state-pressed.png)
*Pressed*

![Outlined card, Default state](/assets/card/state-outlined-default.png)
*Outlined, Default*

  ![Outlined card, Active state](/assets/card/state-outlined-active.png)
*Outlined, Active*

  ![Outlined card, Focused state](/assets/card/state-outlined-focused.png)
*Outlined, Focused*

![Outlined card, Hover state](/assets/card/state-outlined-hover.png)
*Outlined, Hover*

  ![Outlined card, Selected state](/assets/card/state-outlined-selected.png)
*Outlined, Selected*

  ![Outlined card, Pressed state](/assets/card/state-outlined-pressed.png)
*Outlined, Pressed*

#### Modifiers

![Card with Header and Footer](/assets/card/modifier-header-footer.png)
*with Header and Footer*

  ![Card with Header and Action](/assets/card/modifier-header-action.png)
*with Header and Action*

  ![Card with Header](/assets/card/modifier-header.png)
*with Header*

![Card with Footer](/assets/card/modifier-footer.png)
*with Footer*

  ![Card without Header and Footer](/assets/card/modifier-without-header-footer.png)
*without Header and Footer*

### Guidelines

#### Group

##### Spacing between cards

The spacing between cards on the page should follow the global rules of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**. This should be used for both vertical and horizontal spacing between cards on a page.

![Cards spaced apart following the L:24px / M:16px / S:12px spacing rules](/assets/card/group-spacing-between-cards.png)

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

Cards also follow the general spacing rules for each viewport. So we’ll have an inner padding of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**

![Responsiveness, Large](/assets/card/responsiveness-large.png)
*Responsiveness, Large*

  ![Responsiveness, Medium](/assets/card/responsiveness-medium.png)
*Responsiveness, Medium*

  ![Responsiveness, Small](/assets/card/responsiveness-small.png)
*Responsiveness, Small*

#### Interaction

##### Expandable card

Expandable cards have an expand button placed on the top right corner or on the top left corner.

Placing the expand button on the top right corner can be helpful to achieve a better alignment between the card title and the card content.

Placing the expand button in the top left corner can be helpful when the expandable card also has an action placed in the top right corner.

When closed they should have the height of the header.

![Expandable card shown collapsed and expanded, with the expand button in the top right and top left corner](/assets/card/interaction-expandable.png)

##### Draggable card

Draggable cards have a drag button, which uses the drag\_indicator icon, placed in the top left corner.

![Draggable card with a drag button in the top left corner](/assets/card/interaction-draggable.png)

##### Draggable expandable card

Expandable draggable cards have a drag button, which uses the drag\_handle\_corner icon, placed on the top left corner.

Expandable draggable cards have an expand button placed on the top right corner or on the top left corner.

Placing the expand button on the top right corner can be helpful to achieve a better alignment between the card title and the card content.

Placing the expand button in the top left corner can be helpful when the expandable card also has an action placed in the top right corner.

When closed they should have the height of the header.

#### Spacing

Cards follow the general spacing rules for each viewport, so we’ll have an inner padding of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px.** These rules are also applied to the space between the card header and the card content except when used with a **borderless** header. In this case, the card content top padding should be **0px.**

##### Header with bottom border

![Header with bottom border, Large](/assets/card/header-border-large.png)
*Header with bottom border, Large*

  ![Header with bottom border, Medium](/assets/card/header-border-medium.png)
*Header with bottom border, Medium*

  ![Header with bottom border, Small](/assets/card/header-border-small.png)
*Header with bottom border, Small*

##### Borderless header

![Borderless header, Large](/assets/card/borderless-large.png)
*Borderless header, Large*

  ![Borderless header, Medium](/assets/card/borderless-medium.png)
*Borderless header, Medium*

  ![Borderless header, Small](/assets/card/borderless-small.png)
*Borderless header, Small*

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Card`and `Cobalt Design System > Patterns > CardPattern`

* [CardPattern](https://www.figma.com/file/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/3---%E2%9A%97%EF%B8%8F-Patterns?node-id=523%3A485210\&t=jUe1rZb3NiVaRLjg-1) — Patterns library
* [Card handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=12%3A17460\&t=P3SljvXoMZOLHrzs-1) — Handoff guidelines

The Card pattern is available under **Cobalt Design System › Patterns › [CardPattern](https://www.figma.com/design/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/?node-id=523-485210)**.

narrative.markdown:
Checkboxes are used to allow users to select any number of options, simultaneously.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Variants

***Examples*** *illustrating a component’s named variation, states, and other dimensions like sizes, colors, content, etc, preferably paired with and rendered by code instead of presented via static images.*

#### Sizes

One size variation

![Checkbox example — Variants Sizes](/assets/checkbox/variants-sizes.png)

#### States

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Theming

From a design system implementation, the Checkbox element/component variations will depend on the scoped context in which they are going to be used as this may affect sizing, color, and behavior as well. In parallel, a markup implementation should also be discussed within the team as this may affect how the component will be styled.

### Variants

Optionally, checkboxes can have their own text hint under the checkbox label.

Checkboxes must be grouped the same set of options under the same `name` attribute and link the `label` to the corresponding `id` of each checkbox to increase the clickable area.

### Guidelines

Checkboxes are a visual and actionable element mean to represent and to allow a user to change a certain information/option/query's' state (checked, unchecked or even mixed). As opposed to toggles (which in our implementation should roughly equate to a switch), checkboxes are form-contained controls and are able to represent both visually and value-wise more than two states.

### Behavior

#### Internationalization

When it comes to i18n concerns the checkbox element itself does not require any special attention, but instead, the label either next to it (id-matching) or surrounding it should have the appropriate copy alongside with any specific description in the end-users language (either matching user-defined preferences or resorting to following the system-wide adopted language).

#### Spacing

![Checkbox example — Variants Spacings](/assets/checkbox/variants-spacings.png)

### Resources

Find this component under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Checkbox`

For ease of reading, follow all the specifications for the checkbox component from the base to all variations inherent in it.

### Content

* Checkboxes must all be labeled. Write clear, positive, active, concise, and distinct labels. The biggest usability problems for checkboxes and radio buttons come from labels that are vague, misleading, or describe options that are difficult to understand.
* Use sentence case.
* Avoid punctuation, unless you’re using more than one sentence.
* Avoid negative statements (e.g., *Don’t send me any emails*): the user shouldn’t have to check a box to make something not happen. **Exception:** negative phrasing can make sense for checkboxes referring to repeated messages (e.g., *Don't show this message again*).
* If there's more than option available, use *Select* to refer to the user’s action towards a checkbox. Avoid words like *check*, *uncheck* or *click*, because they can be ambiguous.
* Place labels to the right side of checkboxes. **Exception:** for RTL (Right-to-Left) languages, such as Arabic and Hebrew, labels should appear to the left of checkboxes.
* Make the checkbox and the label clickable: a bigger target is faster to click.

**Do:** Use positive statements.
![Do example](/assets/checkbox/do.png)

**Don't:** Avoid negative statements.
![Don't example](/assets/checkbox/dont.png)

### Accessibility

As mentioned above checkboxes are meant to be used within a certain context (a form) and should either be a sibling to a label with a matching ID property or contained/wrapped by a label as this provides assistive tools with a better description of what the element is, what states it can cycle through, what state the element is representing in any given time.

It is still not clear at this time if we are going to resort to a styled approach to the native implementation of a checkbox but if not we must expose the element as having a checkbox role in the operating system's accessibility API and When the aria-checked value changes, fire an accessible state changed event.

More granularly:

* The checkbox element must have a checkbox role.
* The checkbox must have an accessible label provided by one of the following:
  * Visible text content contained within the element with role checkbox;
  * A visible label referenced by the value set by aria-labelledby on the element with role checkbox;
  * aria-label set on the element with role checkbox.
* When checked, the checkbox element has state aria-checked set to true;
* When not checked, it has state aria-checked set to false;
* When “partially” checked, the state aria-checked is set to mixed;
* A set of checkboxes is to be represented as a logical group with a visible label, the checkboxes are included in a wrapping element/container with role group that has the property aria-labelledby set to the ID of the element containing the label.

narrative.markdown:
Can be used to select dates in the near future or past.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

The DatePicker gives users the ability to choose dates from a visual calendar that’s consistently applied wherever dates need to be selected across Talkdesk products.

### Anatomy

![Datepicker example — Anatomy](/assets/datepicker/anatomy.png)

1. **Previous and next month selectors** - To move forward or backward one month at a time
2. **Month selector** - Choose the specific month
3. **Year selector** - Choose the specific year
4. **Weekday indicator** - Days of the week
5. **Day indicator** - Days in the month
6. **Current date indicator** - Specify the current date to the user
7. **Selected range highlight**
8. **Selected range start date**
9. **Selected range start end**

![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: With Navigation (Default)](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-with-navigation-default.png)
*With Navigation (Default)*
The default stage of the DatePicker.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Selected Day](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-selected-day.png)
*Selected Day*
The day selected by the user.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Disabled Days](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-disabled-days.png)
*Disabled Days*
Days that aren't available to be picked.

![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Highlighted Days](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-highlighted-days.png)
*Highlighted Days*
Depending on the case, you could highlight specific days to inform the user about relevant days to be picked.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: With Today Highlighted](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-with-today-highlighted.png)
*With Today Highlighted*
A visual reminder about the current day.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Starting On A Different Weekday](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-starting-on-a-different-weekday.png)
*Starting On A Different Weekday*
Usually, the weekday starts on Sundays. However, this can be customized.

![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Custom Weekdays](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-custom-weekdays.png)
*Custom Weekdays*
As a default behavior, the DatePicker weekdays are written in English. However, this can be customized to support different languages.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: Custom Months](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-custom-months.png)
*Custom Months*
As a default behavior, the DatePicker months are written in English. However, this can be customized to support different languages.

  ![Datepicker example — Variants Modifiers: With TimePicker](/assets/datepicker/modifiers-with-timepicker.png)
*With TimePicker*
You can use the DatePicker with the TimePicker component, a common use case mapped as our DatePickerPattern.

#### Position

##### Below input

The DatePicker will be opened below the originated input as default.

![Datepicker example — Position Below input](/assets/datepicker/position-below-input.png)

##### Above input

It also can be opened from the top when there is no available space on the page to the bottom

![Datepicker example — Position Above input](/assets/datepicker/position-above-input.png)

### Guidelines

#### Use cases

##### Changing the month

Pick a different month in the month button inside the DatePicker or change it manually in the InputGroup.

![Datepicker example — Use cases Changing the month](/assets/datepicker/use-cases-changing-the-month.png)

##### Changing the year

Pick a different year in the dropdown options inside the DatePicker or change it manually in the InputGroup.

![Datepicker example — Use cases Changing the year](/assets/datepicker/use-cases-changing-the-year.png)

##### Technical limitations

Due to some technical limitations, sometimes the user can only select dates within a 30-day range at any given time. A short message informs the user about the condition and blocks the possibility of adding more days to the range period.

Use case for reference [here](https://www.figma.com/file/RhpVFBHRiadKUb6mAeKgKJ/23Spring_Customer-Journey-Analytics?type=design\&node-id=750%3A372428\&t=nSpGD8FbdXBe5qHT-1) (IA).

![Datepicker example — Use cases Technical limitations](/assets/datepicker/use-cases-technical-limitations.png)

##### Selecting a range with invalid dates

Sometimes, users can select a date range that included invalid dates. We allow selecting the range, but the days that are invalid should still appear disabled.

After this, we need to inform the user that those dates will not be considered.

We can due it as a hint under the input or as a message in the UI, according to the use case.

![Datepicker example — Use cases Selecting a range with invalid dates: Range selection with invalid dates](/assets/datepicker/dates-range-selection-with-invalid-dates.png)
*Range selection with invalid dates*

##### Custom option

If you need to add more than one DatePicker with a popup in the same form/panel/page, you should follow these best practices:

**Do**
- If you need a custom item, combine it in one dropdown by providing the custom option and then exhibiting the InputGroup after selecting it.
- When selecting any other option, hide the InputGroup with the custom option.
![Do example](/assets/datepicker/use-cases-custom-option-do-2.png)

**Don't:** Avoid having more than one input to open different DatePickers (e.g. one input for predefined options and another for custom options)
![Don't example](/assets/datepicker/use-cases-custom-option-dont.png)

#### Placeholder

![Datepicker example — Guidelines Placeholder: Single](/assets/datepicker/placeholder-single.png)
*Single*

  ![Datepicker example — Guidelines Placeholder: Range](/assets/datepicker/placeholder-range.png)
*Range*

Related to Filtering, consider following [these](/patterns/search-filtering-and-sorting/) specific guidelines.

#### Best practices

**Do**
- For navigating dates in both the near future or past and the distant future or past, providing multiple ways to select dates.
- Use it when it is useful for the user to see how the selected date is related to other dates and/or which weekday it is.
- Allows to enter the data via the keyboard directly into the input if the user prefers to interact this way.
![Do example](/assets/datepicker/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-do-3.png)

**Don't**
- Don't close after a single date is selected unless a range with a start and end date is required.
- Avoid using it to enter a familiar date, like a birthday. Prefer to use a regular Text Input instead and consider implementing input masking.
![Don't example](/assets/datepicker/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-dont-2.png)

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

When using it isolated:

![Datepicker example — Behavior Responsiveness](/assets/datepicker/behavior-responsiveness.gif)

The content is resized acording to the width.

When using it inside a popup or any element:

![Datepicker example — Behavior Responsiveness](/assets/datepicker/behavior-responsiveness-2.gif)

The component always occupies the width of the content.

#### Interaction

When opening a DatePicker you'll be able to:

* Change the months by selecting the name of the month
* Change the year by clicking on the dropdown
* Choose a specific date or a range

![Datepicker example — Behavior Interaction](/assets/datepicker/behavior-interaction.gif)

#### Dimensions

DatePicker doesn't have a defined width. It always occupies the width of the content, so it will always have the width of the **popup** where it is.

However, we recommend a min-width of `300px` whenever possible.

### Resources

Access this Cobalt component from: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > DatePicker`

* [DatePicker](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?type=design\&node-id=868-79141\&mode=design) — Core components library

* [DatePicker Handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?type=design\&node-id=374-214261\&mode=design) — Specs

* [Calendar](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/calendar--primary-story) — Storybook > Atomic component

* [DatePicker](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/marketplace_marketplace-components-datepicker-stories--default) — Storybook > Marketplace

* [DatePicker Range](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/marketplace_marketplace-components-daterangepicker-stories--default) — Storybook > Marketplace

### Content

### Writing guidelines

This component has no component-specific copy rules yet. For copy rules that apply
everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

DatePicker is built on react-aria's `DatePicker`. The date is typed in segments (day, month and year)
that also change with the arrow keys, and the calendar opens in a dialog with a keyboard-navigable grid.

* Give it a `label`, so the field has an accessible name.
* Core DatePicker selects a single date. Selecting a range is the Cobalt Marketplace
  [DateRangePicker](/components/marketplace/daterangepicker/).

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
Dividers are used to separate spaces visually and to show hierarchy and structure. ### Design > **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. ### Overview Dividers are an aesthetic tool used to **separate spaces and content**. They bring clarity to a layout by grouping and dividing content in close proximity. ### Anatomy ![Divider anatomy: a divider line and an optional label](/assets/divider/anatomy.png) 1. **Divider** - A line that separates the content 2. **Label** - Text that informs the user what to expect ### Variants #### Colors Dividers now support different colors. However, the default color is grey. ![Horizontal divider separating Section A above from Section B below](/assets/divider/color-default.png) *Default* ![Divider with an applied color](/assets/divider/color-applied.png) *Applied* ![Divider on a gray background](/assets/divider/color-gray-background.png) *Gray background* #### Modifiers It can be a simple line or it can have a label. > **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. > **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. #### Orientation The divider can have two orientations: **horizontal** or **vertical**. By default, dividers are horizontal and should be used for separating content vertically. The vertical divider is used to separate content horizontally. > **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. > **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. ### Guidelines #### When to use * Separating sections on a page * Separating items in a list * Creating a visual contrast between 2 sides of a page #### Best practices ##### Dividing sections Use dividers to separate the main sections of a form and put them before the section header. This allows for a clear separation between groups of information that the user must fill in. **Do:** Use horizontal dividers to separate sections inside a form. Can use custom margins of 16px from the top (to make space after the previous form element) and 0px to the bottom (because the section header already has a top margin) ![Do example](/assets/divider/usecase-dividing-sections-do.png) **Don't:** Don't use dividers to separate individual fields as this creates too much "visual noise". ![Don't example](/assets/divider/usecase-dividing-sections-dont.png) ##### Using labels Make the labels short and use them as a clear separator and not as a label for the alternative action(s). Labels are also always **uppercase**. **Do:** Use dividers with labels when you want to clearly identify different parts as alternatives. ![Do example](/assets/divider/usecase-using-labels-do.png) **Don't:** Avoid using large labels. ![Don't example](/assets/divider/usecase-using-labels-dont.png) ### Behavior #### Responsiveness The divider could follow the width (for horizontal dividers) or height (for vertical dividers) of the content it's being separated. #### Spacing By default, there is **no margin** before and after the divider, but this can be achieved by applying the spacer token component of Cobalt. Horizontal dividers always fill the container `width=100%`. ![Horizontal divider](/assets/divider/spacing-horizontal-no-margin.png) *Horizontal with no margin* ![Vertical divider](/assets/divider/spacing-vertical-no-margin.png) *Vertical with no margin* If the spacer is used, then it is recommended that the spacings respect the current grid baseline values. For example, on large screens, we could add a margin of 24px. This margin can be applied to only one side of the divider (e.g. you can have 24px from the top and 0 from the bottom). ![Horizontal divider with 24px margin](/assets/divider/spacing-horizontal-margin.png) *Horizontal with margin* Horizontal dividers can be used to separate any type of content on a page. ![Vertical divider with 24px margin](/assets/divider/spacing-vertical-margin.png) *Vertical with margin* Vertical dividers can also be used to separate columns on a page (e.g: a table on the left and an accordion on the right). ### Resources Access this Cobalt component from: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Divider` * [Divider component](https://www.figma.com/file/OAai6yfKydI1p4afnUUI6V/2B---%F0%9F%93%96-Core-documentation-A-%3E-L?node-id=1003-307424) — Core component library * [Divider handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=197-128950) — Handoff guidelines ### Code ### Installation > **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site. ### Examples ### Props ### Content ### Writing guidelines The only text a divider carries is its optional label. Keep it short and uppercase, and use it as a clear separator between alternatives, not as a label for an action — see *Using labels* in the Design tab. For copy rules that apply everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/). ### Accessibility ### Interactions A divider is not interactive: it takes no focus and responds to no mouse or keyboard input. ### Considerations #### Development The divider should have the proper role assigned to it so that it can be associated with a separator between sections of the page. ```html
``` ### How to test the component * Press `Tab` through the page and confirm focus never lands on the divider. * With a screen reader, confirm the divider is announced as a separator (from `role="separator"`). * Confirm a labelled divider's text is read as plain text, not as a heading or a control.

shrinks to the trigger's content and can clip long options.

[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel).

props.name: download
props.description:

A space-separated list of URLs to ping when the link is followed. See

props.name: referrerPolicy
props.description:
How much of the referrer to send when following the link. See

narrative.markdown:
Dropdowns present a list of items from which a user can select one or multiple options.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

![An open dropdown: the field labelled Dropdown and, below it, the Dropdown Menu listing actions with the selected Value checked](/assets/dropdown/cover.png)

### Overview

Dropdown is used when the user has options to choose from (one or multiple options).

* The dropdown displays placeholder text in the field when closed.
* Clicking on a closed field opens a menu of options.

Selecting an option from the menu closes it and the selected option text replaces the placeholder text in the field and also remains as an option in place if the menu is open.

### Anatomy

The default / activated form of a dropdown.

![Dropdown anatomy: label, hint, field, item, selected item, and dropdown menu](/assets/dropdown/anatomy.png)

1. **Label** - Text that informs the user what to expect in the list of dropdown options.
2. **Hint** - Assistive text to help the user choose the right selection.
3. **Field** - Persists when the dropdown is open or closed.
4. **Item** - A choice for the user, shown with other choices in a menu.
5. **Selected item** - A variation of status for the dropdown item.
6. **Dropdown Menu** - A list of options to choose from, displayed as an open state.

### Variants

#### Sizes

Two sizes available: `Medium` and `Small`

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### States

Fourteen options available: `Default`, `Active`, `Active-placeholder`, `Active-search`,`Placeholder`, `Disabled`, `Error`, `Error-placeholder`,`Dismissible`, `Focused`, `Focused-placeholder`, `Read-only`, `Warning` and `Warning-placeholder`

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Styles

**Border**

`Default` or `Borderless`

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Modifiers

##### By function

`Basic`, `With icon`, `With flag`, `Multi-selection` (with one row), `Nested` and `With presence`

Note: Some variations may not be implemented and available in the Storybook yet.

![Default state](/assets/dropdown/state-default.png)
*Default*

  ![Dropdown modifier examples: with icon, with flag, with a custom icon, and icon on the right](/assets/dropdown/modifier-default.png)
*Icon ON*

![Dropdown example — Modifiers By function: MultiSelect ON - One row](/assets/dropdown/modifier-icon-on.png)
*MultiSelect ON - One row*

  ![Dropdown example — Modifiers By function: Nested ON](/assets/dropdown/nested-on.png)
*Nested ON*

![Dropdown example — Modifiers By function: Right value ON](/assets/dropdown/right-value-on.png)
*Right value ON*

  ![Dropdown example — Modifiers By function: Tag ON](/assets/dropdown/tag-on.png)
*Tag ON*

![Dropdown example — Modifiers By function: Action ON](/assets/dropdown/action-on.png)
*Action ON*

##### By structure

We have different types of similar components.

![Dropdown example — Modifiers By structure: Default dropdown](/assets/dropdown/default-dropdown.png)
*Default dropdown*
Used for creating multiple options to a simple dropdown.

  ![Dropdown example — Modifiers By structure: Item from a dropdown menu](/assets/dropdown/item-from-a-dropdown-menu.png)
*Item from a dropdown menu*
Used for creating selectable options inside a dropdown menu.

![Group title item](/assets/dropdown/structure-group-title.png)
*Group title*
Title for a dropdown item

  ![Load more link](/assets/dropdown/structure-load-more.png)
*Load more*
Loading states for dropdown items

![Dropdown example — Modifiers By structure: Microcopy](/assets/dropdown/microcopy.png)
*Microcopy*
Notes to include in a dropdown menu

![Search bar inside a dropdown menu](/assets/dropdown/structure-search.png)
*Search*
To find for information or data

### Guidelines

#### When to use

Dropdowns can be used in forms on full pages, in modals, or on panels. You can use when:

* Offering a single selection from a list of options.
* Offering multiple selections from a list of options.

#### When not to use

* If there are only two options to choose from. Instead, use a [radio button](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/085bf5-radio-button) group or a toggle.
* If the number of options is indeterminate, use a search field instead.
* Do not nest dropdowns or use them to display overly complex information. Keep option selections as straightforward as possible.

### Behavior

#### Positioning

A dropdown can open up or down depending on its position on the screen. If opened at the bottom of the screen, for example, it will expand upwards to avoid being cropped. By default, our dropdown opens downwards.

#### Minimum width

The width of the Content of the dropdown is by default automatically resized according to the dropdown Input width, however, when using the borderless variation, it can be necessary to customize it.

The width of the Content of the dropdown can be customized by setting the Content viewport property with `Small` or `Medium` values.

#### Max height

The max height for a dropdown menu is implemented as `250px` and beyond that, the scroll will come up for the user.

#### Spacing

Dropdown menus should be positioned at **4px** from the input above. This is already included in the component, so you just need to snap them together (**0px**).

![0px spacing annotation between the dropdown field and the dropdown menu below it](/assets/dropdown/spacing-0px.png)

You can see that there are some dotted lines on the top and bottom of the dropdown background. These are guide rules to position the first and last elements of the list.

You should, try to position the first element until the dotted line disappears.

![Dotted top guide line; an item is positioned to cover the guide](/assets/dropdown/spacing-top-guide.png)

All elements inside the dropdown menu already have the required spacing inside. So you just need to snap them together (**0px**). This also includes the dividers, search bar, loaders, etc.

When finished, make sure to resize the dropdown so that the bottom guide is also covered by the last item in the list.

![First item, selected item, third item, and a Load more link snapped together with 0px spacing; the dropdown is resized so the last item covers the bottom guide](/assets/dropdown/spacing-bottom-guide.png)

#### General

##### Scrolling

Dropdown menu can be scrollable. It is necessary to show a fixed scrollbar inside the list with multiple options.

![Scrollable dropdown menu listing cities, with a visible scrollbar](/assets/dropdown/behavior-scrolling.png)

##### Text truncation

Avoid having multiple lines of text in a dropdown. If it is mandatory, [Tooltips](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/94ad96-tooltip) can be helpful to display the entire content of a truncated text string. If the text is too long for one line, add an ellipsis `(…)` for overflow content, and accompany a tooltip to show the full string of text.

![Dropdown item truncated with an ellipsis, with a tooltip showing the full text](/assets/dropdown/behavior-truncation.png)

##### Actions in the list

Actions in the list could be placed either on top or at the bottom with a divider between them and the list items. The 10K dropdown also gives you the choice to show actions only when you want. So for example, you could show actions only if there are no results, or only on the main list, or always.

![Two dropdown menus comparing actions placed at the top versus at the bottom of the list, with a divider separating them from the list items](/assets/dropdown/behavior-actions-list.png)

When performing a search, the results can also include the actions, but the focus will always be placed on the first item of the results, even if there are actions before it.

![Dropdown search results including actions, with focus placed on the first result item](/assets/dropdown/behavior-actions-search.png)

##### Tree selection

In a dropdown, we can have a scenario where the list values are provided in a tree-like structure to make the hierarchy easier to understand with grouped options. Any data whose entries are defined in a hierarchical manner is fit to use this control.

![Dropdown example — General Tree selection](/assets/dropdown/general-tree-selection.gif)

##### Loading

![Dropdown showing a loading spinner, and a second state showing a 'Couldn't load data' error with a Try again link](/assets/dropdown/behavior-loading.png)

We replace the chevron icon with a loader when trying to load the data, and remove the icon if the loading fails.

![Dropdown example — General Loading](/assets/dropdown/general-loading.png)

The same behavior applies to the borderless dropdown, where the chevron icon is replaced by the loader until the data is loaded.

#### Single selection

##### Search

Standard dropdowns use a search action on top of the list of results. We will use the same type of search from the [Multi-select Input](/components/core/dropdown/), allowing users to start typing directly on the input after it’s focused.

![Dropdown example — Single selection Search](/assets/dropdown/single-selection-search.png)

A search can be performed inside the dropdown. However, due to API limitations, a search can only start after the user types at least 3 characters, however, the UX/UI has no limitations and if possible, we should try to deliver results as soon as the user starts typing.

  There is a 300ms delay after each character is typed before the search starts, to allow for users to type a complete name without having to perform several API search requests.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

The results list should follow the same rules as the ones applied to any list of items in a dropdown.

  Closing the dropdown without selecting anything and reopening will clear the previous search.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/871585-dropdown) — Design tab, image 45.*

![Dropdown example — Single selection Search](/assets/dropdown/single-selection-search-3.png)

If no results match the query, we show a corresponding "no results found" message.

##### Opening

Opening a dropdown with `single selection`.

![Dropdown field before opening, showing an 'All' selected value next to a 'Please select...' placeholder](/assets/dropdown/single-opening.png)

A dropdown can load with an already selected item or with a placeholder.

![Dropdown opened with a search field on top of the results, showing a loading state while searching](/assets/dropdown/single-search.png)

When opening the dropdown, its data can be loaded asynchronously, displaying the corresponding "loading message".

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

✅ After successful loading of the data, it should follow these rules:

  * There can be a group of special actions at the top, separated from the rest of the list. These actions can include:
  * The ability to select "All" items
  * Assigning something to "You" without having to go through the entire list to find your name
  * Displaying recently selected options, like the latest 3 selected countries, to facilitate selecting repeating items more quickly
  * Items should be ordered alphabetically, always starting with the ones with more information (e.g. numbers with friendly name, contacts with name) and only then by the ones with only basic information (e.g. only a number)
  * Due to the 10k initiative, we will load the first 20 (configurable) items, but will display the total number of remaining items at the bottom of the list. Users will need to refine the list by performing a search query.

  The selected item should be displayed at the top of the list, followed by the first 20 (configurable) items (making it a total of 21 items in the list).

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/871585-dropdown) — Design tab, image 49.*

![Dropdown example — Single selection Opening](/assets/dropdown/single-selection-opening-2.png)

❌ If the data fails to load, the dropdown closes and an error message is displayed after the input.

##### Selecting items

Navigating and selecting items with `single selection`.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

We can only navigate the dropdown using the mouse.

  After clicking one item, the dropdown closes and assumes the selected option.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/871585-dropdown) — Design tab, image 51.*

![Dropdown example — Single selection Navigation](/assets/dropdown/single-selection-navigation-2.png)

We can have an optional feature of dismissing the selected item directly on the dropdown, after an item is selected.

#### Multiple selection

This will act as an input where the user can perform a search. The search results will be displayed in a dropdown menu under the input. **It will not load a list of items without an initial search**.

##### Search

![Multi-select dropdown with a search field, showing a 'type at least 3 characters' prompt and a loading state while searching cities](/assets/dropdown/multiple-search.png)

A search can be performed inside the dropdown. However, due to API limitations, a search can only start after the user types at least 3 characters, however, the UX/UI has no limitations and if possible, we should try to deliver results as soon as the user starts typing.

  There is a 300ms delay after each character is typed before the search starts, to allow for user to type a complete name without having to perform several API search requests.

![Multi-select dropdown after searching 'Lis', with checkboxes, a Select all option, and Lisbon selected](/assets/dropdown/behavior-tree-selection.png)

After a search is performed, selecting an item will keep the dropdown open and will add a tag to the input.

  Selecting multiple items will keep adding tags until there is available space. After that, it collapses all the remaining item into a "+n" tag.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Search](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-search.png)

A new search can be performed while still keeping the previously selected items.

  The "Select all" option will select all visible items.

  Closing the dropdown without selecting anything and reopening will clear the previous search.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Search](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-search-2.png)

If no results match the query, we show a corresponding "no results found" message.

##### Opening

Opening a dropdown with `multiple selection`.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Opening](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-opening.png)

A dropdown can load with already selected item(s) or with a placeholder.

  If there are more than 2 selected items, an extra item with "+n" is added at the end.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Opening](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-opening-2.png)

When opening the dropdown, its data can be loaded asynchronously, displaying the corresponding "loading message".

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Opening](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-opening-3.png)

✅ After successful loading of the data, it should follow these rules:

  * There is always a "select all" option at the top of the list
  * Items should be ordered alphabetically, always starting with the ones with more information (e.g. numbers with friendly name, contacts with name) and only then by the ones with only basic information (e.g. only a number)
  * Due to the 10k initiative, we will load the first 20 (configurable) items, but will display the total number of remaining items at the bottom of the list. Users will need to refine the list by performing a search query.

  The selected item(s) are kept on their current position, even if they are not in the first 20 items displayed.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Opening](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-opening-4.png)

❌ If the data fails to load, the dropdown closes and an error message is displayed after the input.

##### Tag maximum width

To prevent tag content from being cropped, we set a maximum width of **120px** for the text box.

In a scenario when you have an option selected with a long text, the tag in the multidropdown input adds an ellipsis (…)

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Tag maximum width](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-tag-maximum-width.png)

If the tag group width is greater than the input width, the tag width is 50% of the input width (without the dropdown icon and the third tag) and the tag value uses an ellipsis.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Tag maximum width](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-tag-maximum-width-2.png)

##### Select all

The “select all” option can be added as a special item in a group on top of the list. When active, all items become activated, and when having more than 2 items a +1 tag is also added.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Select All](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-select-all.gif)

##### Selecting items

Navigating and selecting items with `multiple selection`.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Navigation](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-navigation.png)

In v1, we can only navigate the dropdown using the mouse.

  After clicking one item, a corresponding chip is added to the input and the dropdown keeps opened.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Navigation](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-navigation-2.png)

The "Select all" action selects all visible items. Any item that is not loaded into the list is not going to be selected.

##### Dismissing items

Items can be dismissed by clicking the dismiss “X” icon on each item.

![Dropdown example — Multiple selection Dismissing items](/assets/dropdown/multiple-selection-dismissing-items.gif)

#### Interaction

If a dropdown is placed at the bottom of a screen the dropdown items should open upwards.

![Dropdown example — Behavior Interaction](/assets/dropdown/behavior-interaction.png)

#### Internationalization

For RTL (right-to-left) languages, the layout of the dropdown is mirrored. All texts are right-aligned while icons like the chevron and checkmark are left-aligned.

![Dropdown example — Internationalization](/assets/dropdown/internationalization.png)

### Writing guidelines

Make sure all menu items:

* Have accurate, concise and informative labels.
* Use sentence case.
* Remain in a single line of text.
* Avoid articles. E.g., write *Add contact* instead of *Add a contact*.
* For action menu items, use verbs and verb phrases to describe the action that occurs when the item is chosen. For example, *Delete contact* or *Edit*.
* All dropdowns should be sorted alphabetically if no other field is defined by default.
* In most cases, links should be nouns. For example, *Profile* or *Keyboard* shortcuts.

**Do:** Concise yet informative dropdown.
![Do example](/assets/dropdown/do.png)

**Don't:** No need to be repetitive. Items should use sentence case.
![Don't example](/assets/dropdown/dont.png)

### Accessibility

### Interactions

#### Mouse

Clicking a closed field opens the menu of options; clicking an item selects it and closes the menu.
No additional guidance beyond a native interactive element's default behavior applies here.

#### Keyboard

| **Keys**         | **Interaction**                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Backspace/delete | Removes selected item near the insert point                                                         |
| Down arrow (⬇)   | Moves downward in the list                                                                          |
| End              | Goes down to the last item in the list (the last item of the current page if the list is paginated) |
| Enter (↵)        | Selects the list item in the dropdown that is already pre-selected                                  |
| Esc              | Closes the dropdown menu                                                                            |
| Home             | Goes up to the first item in the list                                                               |
| Left arrow (⬅)   | Navigate between the selected items on the input                                                    |
| Right arrow (➡)  | Navigate between the selected items on the input                                                    |
| Tab (⇥)          | Dismisses the focus in the input and moves to the next on the page                                  |
| Up arrow (⬆)     | Moves upwards in the list                                                                           |

Both `10K dropdown` and `multi-select input` should use the same keyboard navigation patterns.

The only difference is that when opening the dropdown we will not focus on the first element of the list until the user presses the **down⬇** key. It should only be automatically focused after the user performs a search.

* [Design Patterns for a Dropdown (Listbox)](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices-1.1/#Listbox) — W3C WAI-ARIA

### Considerations

#### Design

* [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/TR/UNDERSTANDING-WCAG20/navigation-mechanisms-focus-visible.html)
* [3.2.2 On Input](https://www.w3.org/TR/2016/NOTE-UNDERSTANDING-WCAG20-20161007/consistent-behavior-unpredictable-change.html)
* [4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/name-role-value)

#### Development

An accessible dropdown is one where you can choose from a list of options and select one or more of them with the correct information exposed to screen readers.

It's important to render the name, state and position of each option in the dropdown. If the user navigates with the keyboard and the dropdown don't focus their options or don't change between them, the user can't interact with the content and gets lost.

* Avoid very long option names to facilitate understandability and perceivability.
* Do not use the same word or phrase at the beginning of a set of options.
* Always include a `label`, even when using the `hidden-label` prop.
* Never use `placeholder` text in place of a `label`.
* Give the dropdown's text input keyboard focus with the `tab` key (or `shift` + `tab` when tabbing backwards).

### How to test the component

* Tab to the dropdown using only the keyboard, open it, and navigate items with the arrow keys.
* Confirm `Esc` closes the menu and `Enter` selects the focused item.
* With a screen reader running, confirm each option's name, state, and position are announced as
  you move through the list.
