examples.code:
import { Modal, ModalTrigger } from "@talkdesk/cobalt-react-modal";
import Button from "@talkdesk/cobalt-react-button";
import Flex from "@talkdesk/cobalt-react-flex";
import { ModalPanel, PanelTrigger } from "@talkdesk/cobalt-react-panel";

const [container, setContainer] = useState(null);

<ModalTrigger>
  <Button type="secondary">Open fill modal</Button>
  <Modal
    size="fill"
    aria-label="Fill modal"
    isDismissible
    dialogRef={setContainer}
    accessibilityLabels={{ close: "Close modal" }}
  >
    {/* Positioned wrapper so the side panel is clipped to the dialog's
        rounded corners instead of the viewport. */}
    <Flex direction="column" grow forwardedRef={setContainer} style={{ position: "relative", overflow: "hidden" }}>
      <Flex gap={2} padding={6}>
        <ModalTrigger>
          <Button type="primary">Open modal</Button>
          <Modal size="small" aria-label="Smaller modal" container={container}>
            {({ close }) => <Button type="primary" onPress={close}>Close</Button>}
          </Modal>
        </ModalTrigger>
        <PanelTrigger>
          <Button type="secondary" variation="outline">Open side panel</Button>
          <ModalPanel aria-label="Left side panel" position="start" size="small" container={container} isDismissible>
            <Flex padding={6}>Left side panel</Flex>
          </ModalPanel>
        </PanelTrigger>
      </Flex>
    </Flex>
  </Modal>
</ModalTrigger>;

narrative.markdown:
Use modals to complete subtasks or provide critical information while maintaining the context of the underlying page

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Modals are used to present critical information or request user input needed to complete a user’s workflow. Modals interrupt a user’s workflow by design.

When active, a user is blocked from the on-page content and cannot return to their previous workflow until the modal task is completed or the user dismisses the modal. While effective when used correctly, modals should be used sparingly to limit the disruption to the user.

##### Require an immediate response from the user

Use a modal to request information that is preventing the system from continuing a user-initiated process.

##### Notify the user of urgent information

Use a modal to notify the user of urgent information concerning their current work. Modals are commonly used to report system errors or convey a consequence of a user’s action.

##### Confirm a user decision

Use a modal to confirm user decisions. Clearly describe the action being confirmed and explain any potential consequences that it may cause. Both the title and the button should reflect the action that will occur. If the action is destructive or irreversible then use an error modal.

### Anatomy

The default form of a modal.

![Modal example — Anatomy](/assets/modal/anatomy-2.png)

1 - **Header**: Includes a title, optional label, and optional description.

2 - **Body**: Contains the information and/or controls needed to complete the modal’s task. It can include message text and components.

3 - **Footer**: Contains the main actions needed to complete or cancel the modal task.

4 - **X**: The close `x` icon will close the modal without submitting any data. Should not be used for Alert and Error Modal variations.

5 - **Overlay**

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are three responsive modal sizes: small, medium, and large.

* Large modals can be used only in large viewports.
* Medium modals can be used only in medium and large viewports.
* Small modals can be used in all viewports.

Modals have,

* fixed width, dependent of their type and size.
* height proportional to the amount of content up to a 75% of the container height.

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Large](/assets/modal/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Medium](/assets/modal/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Small](/assets/modal/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

#### Types

##### Default modal

* Large modal width = 900px
* Medium modal width = 600px
* Small modal width = 405px

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Large](/assets/modal/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

  ![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Medium](/assets/modal/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

  ![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Small](/assets/modal/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

##### Alert modal

Alert modals are used to validate user decisions or to gain secondary confirmation from the user. Should never be dismissible.

* In large viewports use large alert modal width = 405px
* In medium viewports use medium alert modal width = 405px
* In small viewports use small alert modal width = 320px

![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert - Medium](/assets/modal/modal-alert-medium.png)
*Alert - Medium*

  ![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert - Small](/assets/modal/modal-alert-small.png)
*Alert - Small*

![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert - Large](/assets/modal/modal-alert-large.png)
*Alert - Large*

The alert modal width can increase only when a significative sized component needs to be integrated in the empty state, such as; Cards, TextArea, ProgressBar, Stepper, Rating, SelectionGroup, Slider, Message, among others.

* In large viewports use large alert modal width = 600px
* In medium viewports use medium alert modal width = 600px
* In small viewports use small alert modal width = 320px

![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert with component - Medium](/assets/modal/modal-alert-with-component-medium.png)
*Alert with component - Medium*

  ![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert with component - Small](/assets/modal/modal-alert-with-component-small.png)
*Alert with component - Small*

![Modal example — Types Alert modal: Alert with component - Large](/assets/modal/modal-alert-with-component-large.png)
*Alert with component - Large*

##### Error modal

Error modal is a specific kind of alert modal used for destructive or irreversible actions. In the error modal, the primary button is replaced by an error button. They are commonly used in high-impact moments as a confirmation for an action that would cause significant data loss if done accidentally. Should never be dismissible.

* In large viewports use large error modal width = 405px
* In medium viewports use medium error modal width = 405px
* In small viewports use small error modal width = 320px

![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error - Medium](/assets/modal/modal-error-medium.png)
*Error - Medium*

  ![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error - Small](/assets/modal/modal-error-small.png)
*Error - Small*

![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error - Large](/assets/modal/modal-error-large.png)
*Error - Large*

The error modal width can increase only when a significative sized component needs to be integrated in the empty state, such as; Cards, TextArea, ProgressBar, Stepper, Rating, SelectionGroup, Slider, Message, among others.

* In large viewports use large error modal width = 600px
* In medium viewports use medium error modal width = 600px
* In small viewports use small error modal width = 320px

![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error with component - Medium](/assets/modal/modal-error-with-component-medium.png)
*Error with component - Medium*

  ![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error with component - Small](/assets/modal/modal-error-with-component-small.png)
*Error with component - Small*

![Modal example — Types Error modal: Error with component - Large](/assets/modal/modal-error-with-component-large.png)
*Error with component - Large*

### Guidelines

#### Placement

Modals are always placed vertically and horizontally in the center of the container.

![Modal example — Guidelines Placement](/assets/modal/guidelines-placement.png)

#### Use cases

##### Popup in modals

When opening a popup inside a modal it should exceed the modal limits to its max height.

![Modal example — Use cases Popup in modals](/assets/modal/use-cases-popup-in-modals.png)

#### Forms in modals

Forms components in modals should follow the same rules, for sizes and spacings, as regular forms.

Form inputs in modals should have,

* `width=50%` in large modals
* `width=100%` in medium and small modals

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Large](/assets/modal/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Medium](/assets/modal/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Modal example — Guidelines Forms in modals: Small](/assets/modal/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

#### Multi-step modals

Multi-step modals are sequential modals used for a user perform a task. Multi-step modals should have a fixed height that should never exceed the modal max height, 75% of the container height.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/70ebe1-modal) — Design tab, image 26.*

#### Best practices

**Don't:** Don’t use dismissible Alert or Error modals.

**Don't:** Don’t position modals in any other place than in the center of the container.

**Don't:** Don’t use the divider in a modal header if its doesn’t user toolbar or nav.

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

A large modal will scale to a medium modal in medium viewports.

A medium modal will scale to a small modal in small viewports.

Modals follow the general spacing rules for each viewport. So we’ll have an inner padding of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**

![Modal header padding annotated for large, medium, and small viewports](/assets/modal/responsiveness-padding.png)

##### Minimum screen resolution

When the MainApp width is lower than the modal fixed width, the modal `width=100%` respecting the viewport padding.

As an example, the minimum screen resolution supported by Workspace is 424x540px. Since the dock has `width=58px` in Workspace's code (54px in the App Shell Figma component), the MainApp `width=366px`, lower than the small modal fixed `width=405px`. So in this case, must be used an small modal with`width=100%`.

![Modal example — Responsiveness Minimum screen resolution](/assets/modal/responsiveness-minimum-screen-resolution.png)

#### Interaction

##### Triggering

Modals are triggered as a result of a user’s action and are not system-generated. Common components that can trigger a modal include, a button, link, or icon. On a keyboard, selecting `Enter` or `Space` should launch the modal.

##### Focus

Once the modal is open, set the initial focus to the first location that accepts user input. For example, if the modal contains a form, the focus should automatically be set to the first field when opened.

The focus should then remain trapped in the dialog until it is closed. When navigating by keyboard, `Tab` and `Shift-Tab` do not move the focus outside of the modal.

#### Overflow

When the modal content is longer than the modal height then the body section should scroll vertically with the footer remaining fixed in place.

#### Dimensions

##### Max height

Modal max height is 75% of the container.

As an example, for a workspace height = 540px, the MainApp container height = 500px so the Modal max-height = 375px

![Modal example — Dimensions Max height](/assets/modal/dimensions-max-height.png)

### Resources

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Modal`and `Cobalt Design System > Patterns > ModalPattern`

* [Modal](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/Cobalt-Core-Components?node-id=280%3A10411) — Core components library

* [ModalPattern](https://www.figma.com/file/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/3---%E2%9A%97%EF%B8%8F-Patterns?node-id=522%3A475794\&t=d398ZZSyqOzQqJZg-1) — Pattern components library

* \[Modal Handoff]\([https://Handoff](https://Handoff) guidelines) — Handoff guidelines

* [How to use](https://www.figma.com/file/5mn3vArnbe5ENQfZFRKJBL/8---How-to-use?node-id=601%3A92963\&t=wl70yJ2nLt6Y6dYJ-1) — Figma file with component usage examples

* [V1](https://talkdesk.github.io/cobalt-react-components/?path=/story/modal--basic) — Cobalt

* [V2](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/modal--primary-story) — Cobalt

The modal header/footer pattern is available under **Cobalt Design System › Patterns › [ModalPattern](https://www.figma.com/design/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/?node-id=522-475794)**.

Usage examples are available under **[How to use](https://www.figma.com/design/5mn3vArnbe5ENQfZFRKJBL/?node-id=601-92963)**.

### Code

### Installation

> **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Examples

### Props

### Content

#### Alert and error modals

The purpose of an alert and a error modal should be communicated by its title and primary button. Body text is optional.

Titles should:

* Contain a brief, clear question. If a question is inappropriate, a statement is the alternative.
* Avoid apologies (*Sorry for the interruption*), alarm (*Warning!*), ambiguity or redundancy (*Are you sure?*).

Body text should:

* Give **relevant** information to the user (*You can’t undo this action, Deleting this topic will also delete all of its subtopics*, etc.)
* Avoid asking *Are you sure that… ?* because the dialog itself is already a visual representation of that question. Also, users tend to ignore body text information, so the question must always be placed in the title.

Buttons:

* Should be descriptive/self-explanatory. Avoid *No/Yes* or *OK*.
* Primary button on the right side and secondary button on the left.
* The primary button should use the same action verb used in the title. If there’s space you can use the structure Verb+Noun (e.g., *Delete flow*).
* The secondary button normally uses the word *Cancel* (image 1), but it should be avoided when the main action is similar to Cancel (image 3 ).

**Do:** Title and primary button match.
![Do example](/assets/modal/alert-and-error-modals-do.png)

**Don't:** In this case, the reader is obliged to read the title before clicking OK.
![Don't example](/assets/modal/alert-and-error-modals-dont.png)

**Do:** Clear and concise error modal.
![Do example](/assets/modal/content-do-example.png)

**Don't:** Avoid redudant information in the body text.
![Don't example](/assets/modal/content-dont-example.png)

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Design

* [G202: Ensuring keyboard control for all functionality](http://www.w3.org/TR/2016/NOTE-WCAG20-TECHS-20161007/G202)
* [G90: Providing keyboard-triggered event handlers](http://www.w3.org/TR/2016/NOTE-WCAG20-TECHS-20161007/G90)

#### Development

An accessible modal dialog is one where keyboard focus is managed properly, and the correct information is exposed to screen readers.

If the user navigates with the keyboard, and the modal pops up, the user can't interact with the content because the keyboard focus is behind the modal.

HTML and WAI-ARIA can be used to provide the necessary semantic information, CSS the appearance and Javascript the behavior.

##### Labeling

* `aria-labelledby`Use this attribute to label the dialog. Often, the value of the aria-labelledby attribute will be the id of the element used to title the dialog.
* `aria-describedby`Use this attribute to describe the contents of the dialog.

##### Focus management

A dialog has particular requirements for how keyboard focus should be managed:

* **When the dialog appears on the screen, keyboard focus** (whose control depends upon the purpose of the dialog) **should be moved to the default focusable control inside the dialog.**
* **After the dialog is dismissed, the keyboard focus should be moved back to where it was before** it moved into the dialog. Otherwise, the focus can be dropped to the beginning of the page.
* For most dialogs, the expected behavior is that the dialog's tab order *wraps*, so when the user tabs through the focusable elements in the dialog, the first focusable element will be focused after the last one has been reached. In other words, **the tab order should be contained within and by the dialog.**

narrative.markdown:
Usually used associated to tables but also in other use cases when a several amount of content needs to be split into different pages, the pagination enable the user to jump for a different page.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Usually used associated with tables but also in other use cases when several amounts of content need to be split into different pages, the pagination enables the user to jump to a different page.

### Anatomy

![Pagination example — Anatomy](/assets/pagination/anatomy.png)

1. **Previous page action button.** By interacting with this button the user will navigate to the previous page.
2. **Page action button.** By interacting with this button the user will navigate to a specific page.
3. **Truncated action button.** When the number of pages is higher than the number of interactive options a truncated action button is used. This button is always disabled and it is not interactive.
4. **Active page.** This button shows the active page.
5. **Next page action button.** By interacting with this button the user will navigate to the next page.
6. **Jump to.** By interacting with this dropdown button the user could choose to which specific page will navigate.

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are three sizes available (Large, Medium, and Small), each to be applied to the respective viewport.

![Pagination example — Variants Sizes: Large](/assets/pagination/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Variants Sizes: Medium](/assets/pagination/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Pagination example — Variants Sizes: Small](/assets/pagination/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

#### Modifiers

##### With label

Only available for large and medium viewports.

![Pagination example — Modifiers With label: Large](/assets/pagination/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Modifiers With label: Medium](/assets/pagination/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

##### Without label

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without label: Large](/assets/pagination/label-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without label: Medium](/assets/pagination/label-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without label: Small](/assets/pagination/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

##### Without page numbers

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without page numbers: Large](/assets/pagination/numbers-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without page numbers: Medium](/assets/pagination/numbers-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without page numbers: Small](/assets/pagination/numbers-small.png)
*Small*

##### Without jump

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without jump: Large](/assets/pagination/jump-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without jump: Medium](/assets/pagination/jump-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without jump: Small](/assets/pagination/jump-small.png)
*Small*

##### Without background

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without background: Large](/assets/pagination/background-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without background: Medium](/assets/pagination/background-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Pagination example — Modifiers Without background: Small](/assets/pagination/background-small.png)
*Small*

#### Quantity

When using pagination with labels it can have 2, 4, or 6-page action buttons.

Only available for large and medium viewports.

##### 2 options

![Pagination example — Quantity 2 options: Large](/assets/pagination/options-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Quantity 2 options: Medium](/assets/pagination/options-medium.png)
*Medium*

##### 4 options

![Pagination example — Quantity 4 options: Large](/assets/pagination/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Quantity 4 options: Medium](/assets/pagination/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

##### 6 options

![Pagination example — Quantity 6 options: Large](/assets/pagination/options-large-2.png)
*Large*

![Pagination example — Quantity 6 options: Medium](/assets/pagination/options-medium-2.png)
*Medium*

### Guidelines

#### Placement

Pagination should not be fixed positioned. Should only be visible after scrolling, sticked below the content to be paginated. This behavior must also happen when the pagination component is placed inside a panel.

![Pagination example — Guidelines Placement: Placement - Table](/assets/pagination/placement-placement-table.png)
*Placement - Table*

  ![Pagination example — Guidelines Placement: Placement - Panel](/assets/pagination/placement-placement-panel.png)
*Placement - Panel*

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

Pagination left and right paddings follow the general rules for each viewport, **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**

For small viewports, it is not available the variant with a label.

![Pagination example — Behavior Responsiveness: Responsiveness - Small](/assets/pagination/responsiveness-responsiveness-small.png)
*Responsiveness - Small*

![Pagination example — Behavior Responsiveness: Responsiveness - Medium](/assets/pagination/responsiveness-responsiveness-medium.png)
*Responsiveness - Medium*

  ![Pagination example — Behavior Responsiveness: Responsiveness - Large](/assets/pagination/responsiveness-responsiveness-large.png)
*Responsiveness - Large*

#### Spacing

Pagination actions positioned on the left follow the spacing used for small buttons which is usually **4px** between them.

![Pagination example — Variants Spacings](/assets/pagination/variants-spacings.png)

#### Dimensions

For all viewports, the pagination has always a fixed height of 48px.

![Pagination example — Variants Dimensions](/assets/pagination/variants-dimensions.png)

### Resources

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Pagination`

* [Pagination component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?node-id=608%3A29229) — Core component library
* [Pagination handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=408%3A211798) — Handoff guidelines

everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

Pagination renders a `<nav>` landmark, marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`, and announces
the position ("Page 2 of 10") in a live region when the page changes.

* Its labels default to English ("Previous", "Next", "Go to", "Items per page", "Page 2 of 10"). Pass
  translated strings through `accessibilityLabels` in other languages.
* When a page has more than one Pagination, give each an `aria-label` so the landmarks can be told apart.

For guidance that applies to every component, see [Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

props.name: id
props.description:
The element's unique identifier. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/id).

props.name: container
props.description:
Renders the panel inside this element instead of over the viewport, so it
is positioned against — and for `ModalPanel` clipped by — that element.
The element has to be positioned; a `static` container warns in
development. With `shouldPushContent` it is also the flex row the panel
shares with the content, so it has to be a flex or grid container instead.

props.name: isDismissible
props.description: Renders a close button and lets the `Escape` key close the panel.

props.name: hideCloseButton
props.description:
Drops the close button `isDismissible` would otherwise render, for panels
whose own header already offers a way out. `Escape` still closes the
panel.

props.name: shouldPushContent
props.description:
Makes room for the panel instead of covering the page: the panel
becomes a flex child of `container` and the content next to it
shrinks as it opens. Off by default.

Requires a `container` that is a flex (or grid) container. Let the
content grow to fill the row so it is the part that gives way, adding
`min-width: 0` if it holds anything that can't wrap.

The panel does not adapt to a container too narrow for it and the
content: it is clipped, which can hide its close button, and the
content is squeezed to nothing. Turning this off at those sizes, for
example from a media query, is the consumer's responsibility.

A `start` panel is placed first with CSS `order` but stays last in the
DOM, so keyboard and screen reader users reach it after the content.

The panel is as tall as the row, so it suits a row of fixed height
with any scrolling inside the content: in a row that grows with a
scrolling page, the panel scrolls away with it.

props.name: shouldContainFocus
props.description:
Keeps keyboard focus inside the panel. Off by default: a panel without
an overlay sits beside live page content, which the user is meant to
reach. Note that this contains `Tab` only — the rest of the page stays
readable to assistive technology, which is the point of a non-modal
panel.

props.name: isEntering
props.description:

dialog until the animation completes, since moving the screen reader cursor may cause scrolling
that interrupts the animation.

narrative.markdown:
Panel is a component that comes from a side of the screen. It is as place to displays more information or to perform a task related with the information available in the container.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

A panel can have multiple uses, such as:

* Display content that complements the information available in the container
* Perform a task that will impact the container information. e.g. filtering

### Anatomy

![Panel example — Anatomy](/assets/panel/anatomy-2.png)

1. Header
2. Content
3. Footer
4. Overlay

### Variants

#### Sizes

There are three sizes available: Large, Medium, and Small.

![Panel example — Variants Sizes: Small](/assets/panel/sizes-small.png)
*Small*

![Panel example — Variants Sizes: Medium](/assets/panel/sizes-medium.png)
*Medium*

![Panel example — Guidelines Placement: right (default)](/assets/panel/sizes-large.png)
*Large*

![Panel example — Variants Sizes: X-Large](/assets/panel/sizes-x-large.png)
*X-Large*

#### Modifiers

![Panel example — Guidelines Placement: right (default)](/assets/panel/sizes-large.png)
*with overlay*

  ![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: without actions](/assets/panel/modifiers-without-actions.png)
*without actions*

  ![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: without dismissible button](/assets/panel/modifiers-without-dismissible-button.png)
*without dismissible button*

![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: without header](/assets/panel/modifiers-without-header.png)
*without header*

  ![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: without nav](/assets/panel/modifiers-without-nav.png)
*without nav*

  ![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: without overlay](/assets/panel/modifiers-without-overlay.png)
*without overlay*

![Panel example — Variants Modifiers: with scroll](/assets/panel/modifiers-with-scroll.png)
*with scroll*

### Guidelines

#### Group

##### Multiple panels

It is not possible to have two panels simultaneously opened.

##### Header

The panel header is an **H2 Header.** You can find it under PanelPattern in the Patterns Figma library.

![Panel example — Group Header](/assets/panel/group-header.png)

Unless we have a Nav or a Toolbar, usually the Headers **should not** have a bottom border.

![Panel example — Group Header](/assets/panel/group-header-2.png)

If the Header does not have a **Nav** or a **Toolbar**, then the spacing from the top should be **0px**.

##### Footer

Panel footers can be fixed at the bottom of the panel. You can find it under PanelPattern in the Patterns Figma library.

![Panel without a header row](/assets/panel/modifier-without-header.png)

##### Secondary area

It is possible to have both components (panel and secondary area) active.

![Panel example — Group Secondary Area](/assets/panel/group-secondary-area.png)

#### Placement

Panels are usually displayed coming from the right side of the screen (apart from some exceptional use cases). Generally, the height is the entire page size from top to bottom.

![Panel example — Guidelines Placement: right (default)](/assets/panel/sizes-large.png)
*right (default)*

  ![Panel displayed from the left side of the screen](/assets/panel/placement-left.png)
*left*

#### Overlay

To decide if the panel should be used with or without overlay you should ask:

* **Can the user take the tasks only with the information available in the panel?**

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

If yes, you should use the Panel with overlay.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 19.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

If not, you should use the Panel without the overlay.

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 20.*

![Panel displayed from the right side of the screen (default)](/assets/panel/placement-right.png)

A third option could be considered if the user needs all information available in the container to perform the task.

  In this case, the panel should be used without the overlay and also should push the container.

  This option could show responsiveness issues, so it should be avoided.

  This option should only be used for products that don’t support or that are not used in small viewports.

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

##### Padding

Panels also follow the general spacing rules for each viewport. So we’ll have an inner padding of **L:24px / M:16px / S:12px**

![Panel example — Responsiveness Padding: Small viewport and padding](/assets/panel/padding-small-viewport-and-padding.png)
*Small viewport and padding*

![Panel example — Responsiveness Padding: Medium viewport and padding](/assets/panel/padding-medium-viewport-and-padding.png)
*Medium viewport and padding*

![Large viewport and padding](/assets/panel/padding-large-viewport.png)
*Large viewport and padding*

##### Content from external app

When the panel content is from an external app,

* The panel header and footer will follow the general spacing rules for the app viewport size.
* The panel content will follow the general spacing rules for the container size which is small.

![Panel example — Responsiveness Content from external app: Small viewport and small padding](/assets/panel/app-small-viewport-and-small-padding.png)
*Small viewport and small padding*

![Panel example — Responsiveness Content from external app: Medium viewport and small padding](/assets/panel/app-medium-viewport-and-small-padding.png)
*Medium viewport and small padding*

![Panel example — Responsiveness Content from external app: Large viewport and small padding](/assets/panel/app-large-viewport-and-small-padding.png)
*Large viewport and small padding*

#### Interaction

##### Dismissal

There are two options available:

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*panel with overlay*

Once expanded and if it does have an overlay the user must click the close button or any other area out of the panel zone to dismiss it

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 28.*

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)
*panel without overlay*

If it doesn’t have a dark overlay only the close and/or the cancel button can dismiss the panel

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 29.*

##### Container

It is possible to change the Panel content without closing and opening the Panel by interacting with the information available in the container.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 30.*

#### Overflow

When the information inside the panel content is longer than the panel content height, the content section should scroll vertically with the header and footer remaining fixed in place.

![Placeholder: image still to be added from ZeroHeight](/assets/placeholder-image.svg)

*Image to add: [original on ZeroHeight](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/898106-panel) — Design tab, image 31.*

### Resources

Find these components under: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Panel` and `Cobalt Design System > Patterns > PanelPattern`

* [Panel component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?node-id=2911%3A521199\&t=kK7CUBcAfB6TtCOo-1) — Core component library

* [PanelPattern](https://www.figma.com/file/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/3---%E2%9A%97%EF%B8%8F-Patterns?node-id=156%3A452612\&t=o66S4KY7242cafnp-1) — Patterns library

* [Panel handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=199%3A131807\&t=EDFXlUAHAmUkYOLn-1) — Handoff guidelines

* [Filtering](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/538f94-filtering) — Patterns

The panel header/footer pattern is available under **Cobalt Design System › Patterns › [PanelPattern](https://www.figma.com/design/RbiNiZDJelIajXxTjDY72N/?node-id=156-452612)**.

### Code

### Installation

> **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Examples

### Props

### Content

### Writing guidelines

This component has no component-specific copy rules yet. For copy rules that apply
everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

* Manage focus when it opens and allow Esc to close.
* Give it a dialog/complementary role with an accessible name; with an overlay, treat the rest of the page as inert.

For accessibility guidance that applies to every component, see
[Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

props.name: data-co-surface
props.description:
The surface level of the popover, from 0 to 3. Defaults to one level above
the closest surface.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
The name of the component that triggered the popover. This is reflected on the element
as the `data-trigger` attribute, and can be used to provide specific
styles for the popover depending on which element triggered it.

props.name: triggerRef
props.description:
The ref for the element which the popover positions itself with respect to.

When used within a trigger component such as DialogTrigger, MenuTrigger, Select, etc.,
this is set automatically. It is only required when used standalone.

props.name: isEntering
props.description: Whether the popover is currently performing an entry animation.

props.name: isExiting
props.description: Whether the popover is currently performing an exit animation.

props.name: shouldSkipAnimation
props.description:
Whether the popover should appear and disappear without an entry or exit animation. This is
used by components such as PreviewTrigger to skip animations when quickly swapping between
overlays.

props.name: UNSTABLE_portalContainer
props.description:
The container element in which the overlay portal will be placed. This may have unknown
behavior depending on where it is portalled to. @deprecated - Use a parent UNSAFE_PortalProvider to set your portal container instead. @default document.body

props.name: offset
props.description:
The additional offset applied along the main axis between the element and its
anchor element. @default 8

props.name: placement
props.description: The placement of the element with respect to its anchor element. @default 'bottom'

props.name: containerPadding
props.description:
The placement padding that should be applied between the element and its
surrounding container. @default 12

props.name: crossOffset
props.description:
The additional offset applied along the cross axis between the element and its
anchor element. @default 0

props.name: shouldFlip
props.description:
Whether the element should flip its orientation (e.g. top to bottom or left to right) when
there is insufficient room for it to render completely. @default true

props.name: boundaryElement
props.description: Element that that serves as the positioning boundary. @default document.body

props.name: arrowRef
props.description: A ref for the popover arrow element.

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: A ref for the scrollable region within the overlay. @default overlayRef

props.name: shouldUpdatePosition
props.description: Whether the overlay should update its position automatically. @default true

props.name: maxHeight
props.description:
The maxHeight specified for the overlay element.
By default, it will take all space up to the current viewport height.

props.name: arrowBoundaryOffset
props.description: The minimum distance the arrow's edge should be from the edge of the overlay element. @default 0

props.name: getTargetRect
props.description:
Overrides the target element's bounding rectangle. Useful for positioning relative to
a specific point such as the mouse cursor (e.g. context menus) or text selection. @default target.getBoundingClientRect() @param target - The target element.

props.name: onFocusWithin
props.description: Handler that is called when the target element or a descendant receives focus.

props.name: onBlurWithin
props.description: Handler that is called when the target element and all descendants lose focus.

props.name: onFocusWithinChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the the focus within state changes.

props.name: isNonModal
props.description:
Whether the popover is non-modal, i.e. elements outside the popover may be
interacted with by assistive technologies.

Most popovers should not use this option as it may negatively impact the screen
reader experience. Only use with components such as combobox, which are designed
to handle this situation carefully.

props.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
props.description:
Whether pressing the escape key to close the popover should be disabled.

Most popovers should not use this option. When set to true, an alternative
way to close the popover with a keyboard must be provided. @default false

props.name: shouldCloseOnInteractOutside
props.description:
When user interacts with the argument element outside of the popover ref,
return true if onClose should be called. This gives you a chance to filter
out interaction with elements that should not dismiss the popover.
By default, onClose will always be called on interaction outside the popover ref.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the overlay is open by default (controlled).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

narrative.markdown:
A small callout that helps the user complete a task or learn more and open on demand.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Popups are containers used to display transient content such as menus, options, additional actions, and more. This element pops up over all other elements on a page. They visually stand out through drop shadows floating on top of the interface.

### Anatomy

![Popup anatomy: popup container, trigger item, and content space callouts](/assets/popup/anatomy.png)

1. **Popup container** - An area to place content.
2. **Trigger item** - An interactive element that triggers the Popup to open on click, hover, or focus.
3. **Content space** - An area to place all necessary elements.

### Variants

#### Sizes

The Popup height is dependent on its content.

![Small popup, 200px wide](/assets/popup/size-small.png)
*Small*
W: 200px

![Medium popup, 300px wide, the default size](/assets/popup/size-medium.png)
*Medium*
W: 300px

![Large popup, 400px wide](/assets/popup/size-large.png)
*Large*
W: 400px

#### Modifiers

![Standalone popup with a blank content area](/assets/popup/modifier-standalone.png)
*Standalone*

  ![Top and bottom guide lines used to help position items inside the popup menu](/assets/popup/modifier-dropdown-guides.png)
*Dropdown*
Top padding: 4px

![Top and bottom guide lines used to help position items inside the popup menu](/assets/popup/modifier-dropdown-guides.png)
*Guides*
Top and bottom lines to help position items inside the popup menu

#### Position

Popups should be positioned at **8px** from the triggering element. Since the popup can be positioned on all corners, this means that it’s 8px to the left, right, top, or bottom of the triggering element.

![Popups positioned 8px from their triggering element, shown for an icon-only overflow menu and for a labeled Button](/assets/popup/position.png)

### Guidelines

#### Placement

This component should be triggered after clicking on any button/action and should respect the limitations applied by the component position.

#### Best practices

##### Do's

Popups should:

* Keep information simple and succinct.
* Be used when you need to display additional details or items on a page.
* Be triggered by an interactive component (e.g.: buttons).
* Always be positioned next to the interactive element that triggers them.
* Be used for secondary or less important information and actions since they’re hidden until users hit the trigger.

##### Don'ts

* Don’t use it to present critical information needed to complete a workflow. Use the [Modal component](/components/core/modal/) instead.
* Don’t use when the user hasn’t explicitly triggered the Popup to open on click.
* Avoid changing the styles of Popups (borders, colors, size, etc).
* Avoid using too much information inside the Popup.

##### Alignment

**Do:** Align the Popup edge with the trigger button.
![Do example](/assets/popup/alignment-do.png)

**Don't:** Don't randomly place the Popup near the trigger button.
![Don't example](/assets/popup/alignment-dont.png)

### Behavior

#### Interaction

##### Opening

The Popup component allows you to control when you want to close it. Also, it should animate from its source to reinforce the connection between them.

Also, if a Popup is placed at the bottom of a screen, it should open upwards.

##### Dismissing

A Popup can be dismissed by:

* Clicking anywhere outside of the element (including clicking the source again).
* Selecting an option.
* Taking an action inside the Popup.

![Popup example — Interaction Dismissing](/assets/popup/interaction-dismissing.gif)

#### Overflow

Scrolling is usually not needed when using a Popup. However, if needed, then the content area should scroll vertically. Do not scroll horizontally or let content bleed off the page.

#### Spacing

##### Inner padding

In design, Popups have a default inner padding of **16px** for content to live inside. However, you may reset it to 0 or adjust the top/bottom and left/right padding if needed. For example, adding a menu inside a popup will use special padding (see next section).

![Popup content area with 16px inner padding on all sides](/assets/popup/inner-padding.png)

Regarding code, the padding, being an atomic design, is **0px** by default and the padding must be added through a layout component when desired.

##### Popup menus

Popup menus have a **4px top and bottom padding**. In case you are using a popup to display a menu, there are some specific spacing rules for it. The first one is where to place the first item on the list.

You can see that there are some dotted lines on the top and bottom of the popup background. These are guide rules to position the first and last elements of the list.

You should try to position the first element until the dotted line disappears.

![Dotted top guide line for positioning the first menu item; the item is positioned to cover the guide](/assets/popup/popup-menu-top-guide.png)

All elements inside the popup already have the required spacing inside. So you just need to snap them together (**0px**). This also includes the dividers.

When finished, make sure to resize the popup so that the bottom guide is also covered by the last item in the list.

![Three menu items and a destructive action snapped together with 0px spacing; the popup is resized so the last item covers the bottom guide](/assets/popup/popup-menu-list-items.png)

#### Dimensions

##### Max width

Popups are available in three predefined widths: 200px, 300px (default), and 400px. The width can also be configured using the custom variation.

##### Max height

Popups can have an optional max height of 42% and beyond that, the scroll will come up for the user.

### Resources

Access this Cobalt component from: `Cobalt Design System > Cobalt Core Components > Popup`

* [Popup component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?node-id=804%3A49850) — Core Components library

* [Popup handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=197-128952) — Handoff guidelines

* [Dropdown](/components/core/dropdown/) — Popup menu from a dropdown use Popups as a base layer.

* [Tooltip](/components/core/tooltip/) — Tooltips use Popups as a base layer. they have a trigger button, Popup container and text.

* [StatefulPopup](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/marketplace_marketplace-components-statefulpopup-stories--default) — Marketplace library

### Code

### Props

### Examples

### Content

### Introduction

The Popup component is used to display additional information or options that are related to a specific task or section.

### Tone and voice

The tone and voice for the Popup component should be informative, helpful, and occasionally friendly. Be clear and predictable - the content provided should guide users through the additional information or options that are shown on the Popup.

### Word choice

The language used in the Popup should be clear, concise, and easy to understand. Be action-led and use action-oriented words such as "Learn more", "View details", or "Edit" to describe the function of the Popup.

Avoid unnecessary words and articles such as “the”, “an”, or “a”.

Avoid using technical jargon or language that may confuse users.

### Concise and clear writing

The text in the Popup should be short and to the point.

Be concise but still provide enough information so the user can easily find and navigate to the path they desire.

Use bullet points or numbered lists to break up information into easily digestible chunks. Make sure the Popup is visually appealing and easy to navigate, with clear headings and subheadings.

### Examples

##### Do's

* Do tailor the text in the Popup to match the context of the trigger.
* Do use clear and concise language to describe the function of the Popup.
* Do make sure the Popup is visually appealing and easy to navigate.

##### Don'ts

* Don't use technical jargon or language that may confuse users.
* Don't overload the Popup with too much information, as this may overwhelm the user.

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

* Manage focus and position relative to the trigger; support Esc to dismiss.
* Apply an appropriate role (menu/dialog) and set the trigger's `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup`.

For accessibility guidance that applies to every component, see
[Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
A component that shows continuous progress through a process, such as a percentage value. They show how much progress is complete and how much remains.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

Progress bars are feedback that allows the user to know that something is busy loading. They're animated bars that show a rate of completion for a system task or a response to user input.

They can also be accompanied by a percentage of completion value, a label, and a description that could bring more context about the progression.

### Anatomy

![ProgressBar anatomy: label, fill, track, percentage, description](/assets/progress-bar/anatomy.png)

1. **Label**: Text that informs the user what to expect when processing the content.
2. **Fill**: The visual representation of how much remains in the loading.
3. **Track**: The path of the loader.
4. **Percentage**: The percentage of how much progress is complete.
5. **Description**: Gives context about the progression.

### Variants

#### Sizes

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Colors

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Modifiers

![Isolated ProgressBar, no label or description](/assets/progress-bar/modifier-isolated.png)
*Isolated*

  ![ProgressBar with description](/assets/progress-bar/modifier-with-description.png)
*With Description*

  ![ProgressBar with label and percentage](/assets/progress-bar/modifier-with-label.png)
*With Label*

#### Progress

Preview of the percentage change just for reference in Figma simulating the progress indicator.

![ProgressBar at 0%](/assets/progress-bar/progress-0.png)
*0%*

![ProgressBar at 25%](/assets/progress-bar/progress-25.png)
*25%*

![ProgressBar at 50%](/assets/progress-bar/progress-50.png)
*50%*

![ProgressBar at 75%](/assets/progress-bar/progress-75.png)
*75%*

![ProgressBar at 100%](/assets/progress-bar/progress-100.png)
*100%*

#### Theming

The ProgressBar remains the same across themes, only changing through the color categories.

### Guidelines

#### When to use

* Use it when a file is downloading.
* Use it when a file is uploading.
* For a long-running process or background process, e.g. importing data or exporting reports.
* Use it to provide context or orientation within the process.
* Use it to provide some idea of how long the process is.

![Example of a ProgressBar being used when a file is uploading. The user needs to wait to continue.](/assets/progress-bar/usage-uploading.png)

Example of a ProgressBar being used when a file is uploading. The user needs to wait to continue.

![After the progression is complete, the user can proceed.](/assets/progress-bar/usage-complete.png)

After the progression is complete, the user can proceed.

#### When not to use

* Don't use it for loading small components.
* Don't use it for inline loading.
* Don't use it for loading multiple components.
* Don't use it to give feedback for an entire page load.
* Don't use it to inform about what’s to come.

Please also consider checking the [Color | Color usage](https://zeroheight.com/51aaf6147/p/49728f/b/94c676) page when applying different colors in the ProgressBar.

#### Placement

In general, you need to place the ProgressBar very close to the content that is being loaded. The ProgressBar span the full width. You can make it more or less obvious to a user. As a general rule of thumb, pages with a short load time can have a more subtle loader, while pages with a lengthy load time need the ProgressBar to be more apparent.

![ProgressBar sizes preview](/assets/progress-bar/placement.png)

#### Comparison between components

##### ProgressBar vs skeleton

If you want a more specific loading experience focused on the page structure you should use a [Skeleton](https://designsystem.talkdesk.com/51aaf6147/p/243842-skeleton) to represent loading content better. The simplest view of the page loads first, followed by progressively more detailed batches until the entire viewport has loaded.

##### ProgressBar vs 3Dots

3Dots is the loader Workspace shows while a whole app loads; apps can't use it (see
[App loading](/workspace/app-loading/)). For fast processes that take less than 300ms, consider no loading
state at all.

##### ProgressBar vs spinner

Consider using a Spinner for a tiny, inline action or feedback, e.g. clicking a button and the action will take time.

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

ProgressBar has three sizes, each one to be used in the respective viewport. The height of the ProgressBar can be customized by setting the viewport property with `Small`, `Medium` or `Large` values.

#### Internationalization

For RTL (right-to-left) languages, the layout of the ProgressBar is mirrored. The label is right-aligned, the percent value is left-aligned, and the fill progresses from right to left. Keep in mind that the placement of the percent sign differs depending on the region.

![Progress bar example — Internationalization](/assets/progress-bar/internationalization.png)

### Resources

Find this component under: `Cobalt Design System > Core Components > ProgressBar`

* [ProgressBar Component](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Core-Components?node-id=734%3A41948) — Core Components library
* [ProgressBar Handoff](https://www.figma.com/file/o1okDlSciNFIyJzEmB7Vws/5---%F0%9F%94%8D-Handoffs?node-id=277%3A178106) — Component specs

### Code

### Installation

> **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Examples

### Props

### Content

Use simple, clear, and unambiguous labels.

![Do example](/assets/progress-bar/content-do-1.png)
*Do*

![Do example](/assets/progress-bar/content-do-2.png)
*Do*

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

* Renders a native `<progress>`, exposing value/max to assistive tech.
* Provide an associated label; for indeterminate states, omit `value`.

For accessibility guidance that applies to every component, see
[Accessibility](/foundations/accessibility/overview/).

narrative.markdown:
The Radio button lists are used to allow a user to select a single option from a list of visible options.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Variants

***Examples*** *illustrating a component’s named variation, states, and other dimensions like sizes, colors, content, etc, preferably paired with and rendered by code instead of presented via static images.*

#### Sizes

One fixed size

![Radio example — Variants Sizes](/assets/radio/variants-sizes.png)

#### States

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Theming

From a design system implementation, the Radio element/component variations will depend on the scoped context in which they are going to be used as this may affect sizing, color, and behavior as well. In parallel, a markup implementation should also be discussed within the team as this may affect how the component will be styled.

### Variants

Optionally, radios can have their own text hint under the radio label.

Radios must be grouped the same set of options under the same `name` attribute and link the `label` to the corresponding `id` of each radio to increase the clickable area.

### Guidelines

Much like checkboxes, radio is a visual and actionable element mean to represent and to allow a user to change a certain information/option/query's' state (but in this case making so that it holds a value, for a wrapping/surrounding radio-group, picked by the user). Similarly to checkboxes radio buttons should also be scoped within a form and furthermore in a radio group.

### Behavior

#### Internationalization

The radio element itself does not require special efforts when it comes to i18n implementation or concerns, but rather, the label either id/name-matching or surrounding them should have the appropriate copy alongside any specific description in the end-users language (either matching user-defined preferences or resorting to following the system-wide adopted language).

#### Spacing

![Radio example — Variants Spacings](/assets/radio/variants-spacings.png)

* [FormCheck](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/Cobalt-Core-Components?node-id=1087%3A347610) — Cobalt Core Component

* [V1](https://talkdesk.github.io/cobalt-react-components/?path=/story/form-elements-checkboxes-radio-radio--checked) — Cobalt

* [V2](https://prd-cdn-talkdesk.talkdesk.com/cobalt/docs/index.html?path=/docs/input--primary-story#radio) — Cobalt

### Group

To add a radio group, should be used the component FormCheck. The main guideline for this component is to **select the first option of the radio button by default**.

![Radio example — Group](/assets/radio/group.png)

📌 [Reading reference - Radio buttons: Always select one?](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/radio-buttons-default-selection/)

Radio buttons and checkboxes already have the required spacing to the right and to the bottom to allow creating groups of items.

You can just snap them together vertically or horizontally.

![Radio example — Group](/assets/radio/group-2.png)

### Code

### Installation

> **Interactive demo — Install.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Examples

### Props

### Content

* Radio buttons must all be labeled. Write clear, positive, active, concise, and distinct labels. The biggest usability problems for radio buttons come from labels that are vague, misleading, or describe options that are difficult to understand.
* Use sentence case.
* Avoid punctuation, unless you’re using more than one sentence.
* Avoid negative statements (e.g., *Don’t send me any emails*): the user shouldn’t have to select a radio button to make something not happen.
* Use *Select* to refer to the user’s action towards a radio button. Avoid words like *check*, *uncheck* or *click*, because they can be ambiguous.
* Make the button and the label clickable: a bigger target is faster to click.

**Do:** Use of "Select", sentence case and a write a clear and concise label.
![Do example](/assets/radio/do.png)

**Don't:** Avoid words like "click".
![Don't example](/assets/radio/dont.png)

### Accessibility

The attribute “value” is the unique value associated with each radio button. Although the value is not shown to the end-user, but is sent to the server on "submit" to identify which radio button value/option was selected.

Radio buttons must be used within a certain context (a form) and should either be sibling to a label with a matching name property or contained/wrapped by a label as this provides assistive tools with a better description of what the element is, what state of selection it represents at a given time.

As of this time there is no markup implementation on Cobalt V2 or suggested approach so, more granularly:

* The radio-button currently checked in a group or unchecked is identified using `aria-checked=“true”` and `aria-checked=“false”` respectively;
* Only one radio button can be selected at a time, all other radio buttons in a group should define `aria-checked=”false”`;
* The label for the radio group is defined using `aria-labelledby` attribute;
* `div` element with role `radio` has `onkeydown` event to support keyboard activation of the radio.
* `div` element with role `radio` has `tabindex="0"` to become part of the tab order of the page.
* Each radio has `tabindex="-1"` except one.
* The state of selection must be visually indicated (e.g. checked, unchecked). To ensure the visual state representation is visible when browsers or operating system use “High Contrast” settings by people with any type visual impairments; The visual representations must be implemented in CSS rather than through use of a background images. (as CSS background image techniques yield disappearing/non-usabe visual representations when browsers or operating systems are set to display high contrast themes/modes)
* `setRadioButton` function uses `aria-checked` attribute to make sure the information communicated to assistive technology is the same as the visual state. (e.g. `img` element)
* `onfocus` and `onblur` event handlers on `radio` support visual focus styling for keyboard only users.

narrative.markdown:
SearchInput allows users to enter a word or phrase to find relevant content.

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

### Overview

SearchInput allows the user to find relevant content. The user can filter content using different words or phrases as keywords.

### Anatomy

![Search input example — Anatomy](/assets/search-input/anatomy.png)

1. **Label**
2. **Icon**
3. **Hint**
4. **Placeholder**
5. **Dismissible button**

### Variants

#### Sizes

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### States

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

#### Modifiers

![Search input example — Variants Modifiers: Standalone](/assets/search-input/modifiers-standalone.png)
*Standalone*

  ![Search input example — Variants Modifiers: With label](/assets/search-input/modifiers-with-label.png)
*With label*

  ![Search input example — Variants Modifiers: With hint](/assets/search-input/modifiers-with-hint.png)
*With hint*

#### Arrangement

![Search input example — Variants Arrangement: Variable-width](/assets/search-input/arrangement-variable-width.png)
*Variable-width*
e.g. toolbar

![Search input example — Variants Arrangement: Full-width](/assets/search-input/arrangement-full-width.png)
*Full-width*
e.g. small viewports when associated with the toolbar, inside a Panel, and others.

### Guidelines

#### Group

The SearchInput can be combined with other components such as Button, Toggle, Dropdown, InputGroup, and more to improve the search results.

#### Placement

You can use this component inside a Toolbar, Panel, and Form pages.

![Search input example — Guidelines Placement: Toolbar](/assets/search-input/placement-toolbar.png)
*Toolbar*

  ![Search input example — Guidelines Placement: Panel](/assets/search-input/placement-panel.png)
*Panel*

![Search input example — Guidelines Placement: Pages & Forms](/assets/search-input/placement-pages-forms.png)
*Pages & Forms*

#### Use cases

![Search input example — Guidelines Use cases: Search + results](/assets/search-input/cases-search-results.png)
*Search + results*

  ![Search input example — Guidelines Use cases: Search + Popup with items and description](/assets/search-input/cases-search-popup-with-items-and.png)
*Search + Popup with items and description*
Atomic components can be used together

#### Placeholder

The placeholder is mandatory on SearchInput. The default copy is "*Search...*" but you could add more meaning depending on the content of your search.

#### Best practices

**Do:** You can include a label to provide more context. If so, make sure that the label is clear and concise.
![Do example](/assets/search-input/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-do.png)

**Don't:** Search should fit into one line. Do not use multiline search inputs.
![Don't example](/assets/search-input/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-dont.png)

![Do example](/assets/search-input/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-do-2.png)
*Do*
If necessary, provide search orientations. This helps users to find what they are looking for, especially if the searchable items are complex or have some technical limitations.

![Caution example](/assets/search-input/guidelines-do-s-don-ts-caution.png)
*Caution*
It is recommended to have only one search per page. If you need multiple searches, clearly label them to indicate their purpose.

### Behavior

#### Responsiveness

The small size should be used only for small viewports and the medium size can be used for medium and large viewports.

#### Interaction

The dismissible button should appear after the user type any character inside the SearchInput. When clicking on the close icon, the information added is deleted.

![Search input example — Behavior Interaction](/assets/search-input/behavior-interaction.gif)

#### Loading

When bringing the results is taking longer than 1.5 seconds, a loading spinner could be displayed until requests are received. Apply the Spinner loading behavior inside the content to be loaded.

For more context, access the [Spinner](/components/core/spinner/) guidelines.

![Search input example — Behavior Loading](/assets/search-input/behavior-loading.png)

#### Text truncation

When the entered text is too long for the available horizontal space in the field, the text truncates.

![Search input example — Behavior Text truncation](/assets/search-input/behavior-text-truncation.png)

#### Spacing

![Search input example — Variants Spacings](/assets/search-input/variants-spacings.png)

### Accessibility

### Considerations

#### Development

SearchInput is built on react-aria's `SearchField`, so the field is a search box (`type="search"`),
`Esc` clears it and `Enter` calls `onSubmit`.

* Give it a `label` (shown above the field, with optional description, hint and error message), so the
  field has an accessible name.
* Pass `accessibilityLabels.clear` (for example "Clear search"). The clear button has no default name,
  so without it a screen reader announces an unnamed button.

  showing the results has to.

narrative.markdown:
Selection group is a type of interaction used in buttons, where the user has available one or more options in a group

### Design

> **Interactive demo — Playground.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

![Selection group example — overview](/assets/selection-group/cover.png)

### Overview

Selection groups are toggles with the appearance of a button. These toggles can be configured to behave as radio buttons with single selection or as checkboxes with multiple selection.

The Selection group should share a common container to emphasize groups of related buttons.

### Anatomy

![SelectionGroup anatomy: container, item, label, divider, icon, selected item](/assets/selection-group/anatomy.png)
*Anatomy*

1. **Container** - Background box that clusters all the itens in the selection group.
2. **Item** - A choice for the user, shown with other options.
3. **Label** - Text that informs what to expect on selecting that item.
4. **Divider** - A line to create a separation between different parts of the selection.
5. **Icon** - An option to groups different actions that are displayed in a visual and simplified way.
6. **Selected item** - A variation of status for the selected item.

### Variants

#### Sizes

We have a `large` , `medium` and `small` versions. Horizontally, a selection group can grow up to a limited number of options provided by the component.

![Large selection group size](/assets/selection-group/size-large.png)
*Size - Large*

  ![Medium selection group size](/assets/selection-group/size-medium.png)
*Size - Medium*

![Small selection group size](/assets/selection-group/size-small.png)
*Size - Small*

#### Content

`Icon with Label` , `Icon` or `Label` content options

![Content - Icon and Label](/assets/selection-group/content-icon-label.png)
*Content - Icon and Label*

  ![Content - Icon](/assets/selection-group/content-icon.png)
*Content - Icon*

![Content - Label](/assets/selection-group/content-label.png)
*Content - Label*

#### Type

`default` and `outline`

Note: Only one version can be used on the same page.

![Type - Default](/assets/selection-group/type-default.png)
*Type - Default*

  ![Type - Outlined](/assets/selection-group/type-outlined.png)
*Type - Outlined*

#### State

`default`, `selected`, `hover`, `disabled`, `disabled-selected`

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

![State - Disabled](/assets/selection-group/state-disabled.png)
*State - Disabled*

  ![State - Disabled-selected](/assets/selection-group/state-disabled-selected.png)
*State - Disabled-selected*

**Error states**

`error default`, `error selected`, `error hover`, `error disabled`, `error disabled-selected`

> **Interactive demo — Demo.** Not reproducible in text; see the documentation site.

![Variation - Error - Disabled](/assets/selection-group/error-disabled.png)
*Variation - Error - Disabled*

  ![Variation - Error - Disabled-selected](/assets/selection-group/error-disabled-selected.png)
*Variation - Error - Disabled-selected*

**Warning states**

`warning default`, `warning selected`, `warning hover`, `warning disabled`, `warning disabled-selected`

![Variation - Warning - Default](/assets/selection-group/warning-default.png)
*Variation - Warning - Default*

  ![Variation - Warning - Selected](/assets/selection-group/warning-selected.png)
*Variation - Warning - Selected*

![Variation - Warning - Hover](/assets/selection-group/warning-hover.png)
*Variation - Warning - Hover*

  ![Variation - Warning - Disabled](/assets/selection-group/warning-disabled.png)
*Variation - Warning - Disabled*

![Variation - Warning - Disabled-selected](/assets/selection-group/warning-disabled-selected.png)
*Variation - Warning - Disabled-selected*

#### Options

Quantity of options available: `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`,`6`, `7`, `10` and `12`.

![Options - 2](/assets/selection-group/options-2.png)
*Options - 2*

  ![Selection group example — Variants Options: Options - 3](/assets/selection-group/options-options-3.png)
*Options - 3*

  ![Selection group example — Variants Options: Options - 4](/assets/selection-group/options-options-4.png)
*Options - 4*

![Selection group example — Variants Options: Options - 5](/assets/selection-group/options-options-5.png)
*Options - 5*

  ![Options - 2](/assets/selection-group/options-2.png)
*Options - 6*

  ![Options - 7](/assets/selection-group/options-7.png)
*Options - 7*

![Selection group example — Variants Options: Options - 10](/assets/selection-group/options-options-10.png)
*Options - 10*

  ![Options - 12](/assets/selection-group/options-12.png)
*Options - 12*

### Guidelines

A Selection group can be used to allow users to complete tasks that involve making choices such as selecting options or switch settings.

#### IVR

**Studio** is where this component is being most used as they use it to configure IVRs. This is one of the main reasons why we have options 10 to 12 available (considering special characters).

![Selection group example — Guidelines IVR](/assets/selection-group/guidelines-ivr.png)

#### Days of the week

**Admin** is using Selection groups for business hours (selecting the days of the week the contact center is open).

![Selection group used to pick days of the week (MON through SUN)](/assets/selection-group/days-of-the-week.png)

#### Multiple normal

We can have this scenario for example in the **Business hours** configuration page where multiple selection groups are used to set multiple independent working hours.

![Multiple independent selection groups, one per day, used to set business hours](/assets/selection-group/multiple-normal.png)

#### Tab navigation

Everywhere else, is a toggle between two or more actions (mostly used as a tabbed nav).

### Behavior

#### Selecting

##### Single selection

By default, the Selection group acts like a radio button group. In this scenario, only one item can be selected and active at a time. If you select one item, respectively this action will deselects any other.

![Single selection: selecting one item deselects any other](/assets/selection-group/single-selection.png)

##### Multiple selection

Adding the `multiple` attribute allows multiple items to be selected (similar to the behavior of a checkbox). In this mode the values of the toggles are not used.

![Multiple selection: more than one item can be selected at once](/assets/selection-group/multiple-selection.png)

#### Available options

The minimum available options are 2. There is no maximum defined however as a design rule you should try to keep your options under 7 items.

There are exceptions for this if you need to use the selection group for IVR, which will need all the digits 0-9 and also the # and \* characters, making it a 12 options selection group.

#### Positioning

They can be placed anywhere inside the screen respecting the grid from the layout pre-settings.

#### Orientation

They can be rendered only in a **horizontal** orientation.

**Do:** 
![Do example](/assets/selection-group/orientation-do.png)

**Don't:** 
![Don't example](/assets/selection-group/orientation-dont.png)

#### Appearance

The appearance of a Selection group will follow the `default` style. If you want to, you can switch into the `outline` style. Just remembering that it is necessary to follow **only one style per page**.

**Do:** 
![Do example](/assets/selection-group/appearance-do.png)

**Don't:** 
![Don't example](/assets/selection-group/appearance-dont.png)

#### Disabled options

A Selection group with options that cannot be selected can either be given a disabled state, or be hidden.

![Selection group example — Behavior Disabled options: Disabled-selected](/assets/selection-group/options-disabled.png)
*Disabled*

  ![Selection group example — Behavior Disabled options: Disabled-selected](/assets/selection-group/options-disabled.png)
*Disabled-selected*

#### Collapsing

When a Selection group is reduced to a width that would cause it to wrap, replace it with a button that opens a Dropdown menu containing the Selection group options in a list to prevent the component from breaking.

![Collapsed selection group replaced by a button that opens a dropdown menu listing the options](/assets/selection-group/collapsing.png)

#### Internationalization

For RTL (right-to-left) languages, the layout orientation of the Selection group is mirrored.

![Selection group in LTR versus RTL orientation](/assets/selection-group/rtl.png)

#### Responsiveness

We have two versions. A responsive one, `full-width`, where each item in the group stretches to fill the space of the container; and a fixed version, `content width`, where each item in the group only stretches to accommodate the content inside it.

### Resources

Find this component under: `Cobalt Design System > Core Components > Selection group`

* [Selection group](https://www.figma.com/file/F3P45YCDsmcmsm01iFIM8s/2---%E2%9A%9B%EF%B8%8F-Cobalt-Core-Components?node-id=575%3A24867) — Cobalt core component

### Writing guidelines

This component has no component-specific copy rules yet. For copy rules that apply
everywhere, see [Grammar and mechanics](/foundations/content/content-grammar-and-mechanics/).

### Accessibility

### Interactions

#### Keyboard

* Users should be able to navigate to the Selection group by using normal keyboard navigation;
* To change the focused item, use the `Left Arrow` or `Right Arrow` keys. Another option to switch between the items is to use `Tab` or `Shift` + `Tab`;
* Selected items should display a visible focus state when users tab to them.

If using the keyboard, the expected behavior:

| **Keys**             | **Interaction**                                       |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter (↵) or spacing | Trigger and activates the select event                |
| Left arrow (⬅)       | Navigate between the selected items to the left       |
| Right arrow (➡)      | Navigate between the selected items to the right      |
| Tab (⇥)              | Dismisses the focus and moves to the next on the page |
| Shift + Tab          | Go back to the previous item (tabbing backwards)      |

### Considerations

#### Design

The Selection group supports the standards for providing accessible web content which are set by the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/).

* [1.1.1 Non-text Content A](https://w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/?showtechniques=131#non-text-content)
* [1.3.1 Info and Relationships A](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)

#### Development

Components need to be accessible to allow its interaction regardless of user's context. The Selection group is accessible by screen readers providing WAI-ARIA, WCAG 2.1 and keyboard support.

* Avoid very long labels to facilitate understandability and perceivability;
* Selection groups should always have one active item;
* If a Selection group contains only icons, you should specify a meaningful label via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` for each of the options available;
* Always include an `aria-label="..."` to describe the intention of the Selection group.
